articles.title: सद्भाव कायमम गर्न सुरक्षा निकायको आफ्नै योजना
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । सुनसरीको देवानगन्जमा आइतबार भएको दुई समूहबीचको झडपपछि विग्रिएको परिस्थिति सामान्य बन्दै गएको छ । सुनसरीबाट मधेसका जिल्लातर्फ परेको बाछिटा पनि कम हुँदै गएको छ ।

स्थिति सामान्य बन्दै गएपछि धनुषा, सिरहा, सुनसरी, सप्तरीमा र वीरगन्जमा लगाइएको कफ्र्यु हटाएर निषेधाज्ञा मात्र जारी गरिएको छ । विशेषगरी अहिले भइरहेको घटनामा सुरक्षा निकायको मूल्यांकन के छ ? अनि तनाव न्यूनीकरण र सद्भाव कायम गर्न सुरक्षा निकायले के गरिरहेको छ त ?

दुई समुदायबीच उत्पन्न तनाव मत्थर पार्न सुरक्षा निकायले विभिन्न रणनीति अपनाएको छ । त्यस मध्येको पहिलो रणनीति हो– उच्च अधिकारीहरूलाई फिल्डमा खटाउने । नेपाल प्रहरीले सुरक्षा व्यवस्था सुदृढ बनाउन ४ एआईजीसहित दुई दर्जनभन्दा बढी उच्च अधिकारीलाई कोशी र मधेश प्रदेशमा खटाएको छ । उनीहरूले त्यहाँको वस्तुस्थिति बुझेर केन्द्रमा रिपोर्ट पठाउने र त्यसैका आधारमा जनशक्ति खटाउने तयारी गरिएको छ ।

प्रहरीका उच्च अधिकारीहरु को कहाँ ?

प्रहरी अतिरिक्त महानिरीक्षक सिद्धिविक्रम शाहलाई बाँके, उमाप्रसाद चतुर्वेदीलाई कपिलवस्तु र ईश्वर कार्कीलाई सुनसरी पठाइएको छ । प्रहरी नायब महानिरीक्षक दिनेशकुमार आचार्यलाई सिरहा र अभिनारायण काफ्लेलाई सप्तरीमा खटाइएको छ ।

प्रहरी वरिष्ठ उपरीक्षक गोपालचन्द्र भट्टराईलाई सर्लाही, सोमेन्द्रसिंह राठौरलाई पर्सा, दीपशमशेर राणालाई रौतहट, नवराज अधिकारीलाई चितवन, कृष्णप्रसाद पंगेनीलाई महोत्तरी र होविन्द्र बोगटीलाई बारामा पठाइएको छ। त्यसैगरी, ज्ञानेन्द्रप्रसाद फुयाँललाई मोरङ, भुवनेश्वर तिवारीलाई धनुषा र अमरेन्द्रबहादुर सिंहलाई मधेस प्रदेशमा खटाइएको छ ।

उनीहरुले विकसित घटनाक्रमअनुसार सुरक्षा व्यवस्थापन गर्ने, जनशक्ति तथा स्रोतसाधन परिचालनको प्रभावकारिता मूल्यांकन गर्ने र आवश्यक नीति निर्देशन दिनेछन् । उनीहरूलाई सुरक्षा योजना कार्यान्वयन, सूचना संकलन र विश्लेषणलगायत जिम्मेवारी पनि दिइएको छ।

सुरक्षा चुक भएको निष्कर्ष

लगातार बसेका सुरक्षा बैठकले सुनसरी घटनामा सुरक्षा चुक भएको निष्कर्ष निकालेका छन्। सूचना संकलन र विश्लेषणमा सुरक्षा निकायले सन्तोषजनक काम गर्न नसकेको बैठकको निष्कर्ष छ । घटनालाई सामान्य रूपमा लिएर बेलैमा नियन्त्रणको प्रयास नगर्दा मानवीय तथा भौतिक क्षति बढेको पनि बैठकको विश्लेषण छ ।

यसैलाई मध्यनजर गरेर सुरक्षा निकायले सीमा क्षेत्रबाट आउने नयाँ व्यक्तिलाई निगरानीमा राखिएको छ । ड्रोनबाट हुने अनुगमनलाई पनि सक्रिय बनाइएको छ ।

दोस्रो सुरक्षा रणनीति हो–दुई पक्षलाई भेट हुन नदिने ।

सम्भावित जोखिम न्यूनीकरण गर्नका लागि तत्काल दुई पक्षलाई टाढै राख्ने गृह प्रशासनको तयारी छ ।

त्यसैगरी सुरक्षा निकायले बनाएको तेस्रो रणनीति हो– सुरक्षा फोर्सको तैनाथी ।

तनाव देखिएका कोशी र मधेशबाहेकका प्रदेशमा पनि अहिले सुरक्षा फोर्सलाई सतर्क अवस्थामा राखिएको छ ।

केही अप्ठ्यारो पर्ने अवस्था आएमा आवश्यक संख्यामा सुरक्षा फोर्सलाई तनाव देखिएका क्षेत्रमा पठाउने तयारी भइरहेको छ । तनाव न्यूनीकरणको चौंथो रणनीति हो– मठमन्दिर तथा मस्जिदहरू रहेका क्षेत्रमा अतिरिक्त सुरक्षा सतर्कता । फिल्डमा खटिन नपर्ने सुरक्षा फोर्सलाई धार्मिक स्थलहरूमा खटाइएको छ ।

अहिलेसम्म प्रहरीले साम्प्रदायिक÷सामाजिक सद्भावमा खलल पुरÞ्याएको भन्दै प्रहरीले ६५ जना व्यक्तिहरू पक्राउ गरेको छ । सिरहमा ५ जना, धनुषामा ४५ जना, सर्लाही ५ जना , महोतरीमा २ जना ,पर्सामा १ जना,सप्तरीमा १ जना ,सुनसरीमा २ जना ब्यक्तिहरु प्रहरीले प्रकाउ गरेको छ । सुरक्षा निकायले कुनै पनि किसिमका भ्रामक सामग्री सम्प्रेषण नगर्न तथा अनावश्यक उत्तेजित नहुन समेत भनेको छ ।

पाँचौँ सुरक्षा रणनीति हो– समन्वयको । प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारीको संयोजकत्वमा जनप्रतिनिधि, धर्मगुरु तथा सुरक्षा निकायले छलफल र समन्वय गरिरहेका छन् ।साथै जनप्रतिनिधि र स्थानीय बासिन्दालाई गाउँ टोलमा नयाँ मान्छे आएमा सुरक्षा निकायलाई खबर गर्न पनि भनिएको छ ।

छैठौं सुरक्षा रणनीतिअनुसार सीमा नाकाबाट घुसपैठ हुनसक्ने परिस्थितिको जोखिम आकलन गर्दै त्यहाँ पनि सतर्कता अपनाइएको छ । सबै सुरक्षा रणनीति प्रभावकारी रूपमा कार्यान्वयन गर्न गृहसचिवको संयोजकत्वमा प्रहरी महानिरीक्षकसहितको कमान्ड फोर्सले एकीकृत सूचनासमेत संकलन गरिरहेको छ ।

सुनसरी घटनाबारे अनुसन्धान भइरहेकाले प्रतिवेदन नआएसम्म दोषी किटान गर्न नसकिने अवस्था रहेको सुरक्षा निकायको भनाइ छ ।

articles.title: निर्मल पुर्जासहित सबै आरोहीको निधन, कस्ता थिए कीर्तिमानी ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । कीर्तिमानी आरोही निर्मल पुर्जासहितका १० जनाकै निधन भएको छ। बिहीबारदेखि हराइरहेका पुर्जाको निधन भएको उनी संस्थापक रहेको संस्था एलिट एक्सपेडले सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत पुष्टि गरेको छ। विश्वविख्यात पुर्जाको निधनले विश्वभर शोकको अवस्था बनेको छ ।

’आज, अत्यन्तै दुःख र मर्माहत हृदयका साथ हामी यो पुष्टि गर्दछौं कि ब्रोड पिकमा गएको हिमपहिरोमा परी निर्मल “निम्सदाइ“ पुर्जाले दुःखद रूपमा आफ्नो ज्यान गुमाउनुभएको छ। साथै, यस अभियानमा संलग्न अन्य सदस्यहरू पनि जीवित रहन नसकेको पुष्टि भएको छ।’ विश्व कीर्तिमानका लागि परिचित पुर्जासहित १० जनाले नै ज्यान गुमाएको घटनाले विश्वभर शोक मनाउन थालिएको छ।

१० जनाले नै गुमाए ज्यान

बिहीबार बिहान करिब ६ हजार ७ सय मिटरको उचाईमा पुगेपछि खसेको हिमपहिरोमा परी उनीहरु वेपत्ता भएका थिए। आरोहण दलको नेतृत्व गरेका पुर्जासहित विभिन्न देशमा आरोहीको खोजी तीब्र पारिएको थियो। हिमपहिरोमा परी ज्यान गुमाउनेहरुमा नेपालका पुरबहादुर गुरूङ, किली पेम्बा शेर्पा ’किलु’, निमा शेर्पा र नवाङ थिन्डु शेर्पा, ओमानका नधिरा अहमद अब्दुल्लाह अल हार्थी, अमेरिकी आरोही मालोरी गाइस, पाकिस्तानका सोहेल साखी र चीनका वाङ जोङ रहेका छन्। तीन जनाको शव शुक्रबार नै फेला परेको थियो भने पुर्जासहित अन्यको निधनको पुष्टी आजमात्रे भएको हो।

निर्मलको भावुक पोस्ट

निर्मल पुर्जाले ब्रोक पिक चढ्नुअघि सामाजिक सञ्जालमा लामो सन्देश लेखेका थिए। उनले ब्रोड पिक चढ्ने योजना नभएको समेत उल्लेख गरेका थिए। तर, उनले प्रार्थना गर्दै लेखेका थिए, ‘ब्रोड पिक– म तिमीसँग केवल एउटा कुरा माग्छु–मलाई सुरक्षित रूपमा माथि पुग्न र फेरि सुरक्षित रूपमा फर्किन देऊ ।’ यहि सन्देशमा उनले कुनै पनि हिमाललाई हल्का रुपमा नलिने जिकिर गरेका पुर्जा अब कहिल्यै नफर्किने गरि अस्थाएका छन्।

‘बेसक्याम्पबाट पहिलो पाइला चाल्नेबित्तिकै मेरो सम्पूर्ण समर्पण त्यही अभियानमा हुन्छ । सधैं त्यस्तै थियो । सधैं त्यस्तै रहनेछ,’ पुर्जाको अन्तिम सन्देश समेत यहि बन्न पुगेको छ ।

पुर्जाले सन् २०१९ मा विश्वका ८ हजार मिटरभन्दा अग्ला सबै १४ हिमाल केवल ६ महिनाभन्दा केही बढी अवधिमा आरोहण गरेर विश्व कीर्तिमान कायम गरेका थिए । ८ हजार मिटर माथिका हिमाल आरोहण रेकर्ड हेर्दा यस पटक ब्रोड पिक चढेका भए चोयुबाहेक ८ हजार मिटर माथिका १४ वटै हिमाल विनाअक्सिजन दुई पटक आरोहण गर्ने विश्व कीर्तिमान उनको नाममा दर्ज हुने निश्चित थियो । अघिल्लो सातामात्र उनले पाकिस्तानको गसेरब्रम २ आरोहण गरी ५७औं आरोहण पूरा गरेका थिए । यस पटक ब्रोड पिक आरोहणको योजनामा भने नरहेको पनि उनले स्टाटसमा उल्लेख गरेका थिए ।

बेलायती सेनादेखि हिमालसम्म

म्याग्दीका निर्मल पुर्जा १८ वर्षको उमेरमै बेलायती सेनामा भर्ति भएका थिए। लामो समय बेलायतमै विताएका उनी बेलायती नागरिक समेत हुन्।पुर्जा १८ वर्षको उमेरमा सन् २००३ मा बेलायती सेनामा भर्ती भएका थिए । त्यसपछि सन् २००९ मा उनी रोयल मरिन्समा आबद्ध भए ।

उनले आफ्ना बुबा र दाजुहरूको बाटो पछ्याएका थिए । उनका बुबा र दाजुहरू सबै गोर्खा सैनिक थिए । गोर्खा सैनिकहरू नेपाली सैनिकहरूको प्रसिद्ध समूह हुन्, जसले २०० वर्षभन्दा बढी समयदेखि बेलायती सेनामा सेवा गर्दै आएका छन् ।

१६ वर्ष बेलायती सेनामा विताएका उनी पर्वतारोहणसम्बन्धि विशेष रुची राख्ने गर्थे। उनको असाधारण पर्वतारोहण उपलब्धिका लागि सन् २०१८ मा तत्कालीन बेलायती महारानी एलिजाबेथ द्वितीयले एमबीई (मेम्बर अफ द अर्डर अफ तजभ ब्रिटिस इम्पायर) सम्मान प्रदान गरेकी थिइन्। यो उत्कृष्ठ उपलब्धिका लागि प्रदान गरिने नागरिक सम्मान भएको बताइन्छ। उनी नेपाली मुलका बेलायती नागरिक भएपनि उनको निधनले नेपाल शोकमा डुबेको छ।

प्रधानमन्त्रीको श्रद्धाञ्जली

प्रधानमन्त्री वालेन्द्र शाहले निर्मल पुर्जासहित ब्रोड पिक आरोहणको क्रममा ज्यान गुमाउनेप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली अर्पण गरेका छन्। प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले लेखेका छन्, ’विश्वको १२औँ अग्लो हिमाल, पाकिस्तानको काराकोरम पर्वत–शृङ्खलामा अवस्थित ८,०५१ मिटर अग्लो ‘ब्रोड पिक’मा विश्व कीर्तिमानधारी निर्मल पुर्जा (निम्स दाइ) सहित छ जना नेपाली तथा अन्य चार विदेशी आरोहीहरूको दुःखद निधनले स्तब्ध बनाएको छ ।

निर्मल पुर्जा लगायत सम्पूर्ण दिवङ्गत आरोहीहरूको भौतिक यात्रा मात्रै रोकिएको हो, तर उहाँहरूको साहस, समर्पण र योगदानको इतिहास सधैँ प्रेरणायुक्त र जीवित रहिरहनेछ ।

सम्पूर्ण दिवङ्गत आरोहीहरूप्रति भावपूर्ण श्रद्धाञ्जली ।’ उसोतः प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले हिमाल आरोहण शिखर चुम्ने यात्रा मात्रै नभई साहस, अनुशासन, त्याग र मानवीय सीमालाई चुनौती दिने अदम्य आत्मविश्वासको सर्वोच्च अभिव्यक्ति भन्दै हिमालले गौरव दिने तर, कहिलेकाँही आफ्नै काखमा सधैका लागि अंगालेर राख्ने बताएका छन्।

उनीहरुको समर्पणको इतिहास कहिल्यै नमर्ने भनेका शाहले शोक व्यक्त गरेका हुन्। उसोतः निर्मलसहितका आरोहीको निधनमा नेपाल शोकमा डुबेको छ भने विश्वभर नै यसको चर्चा र शोक व्यक्तको क्रम चलिरहेको छ।

articles.title: नेपालीलाई झन कडा ! २० हजार डलरको तगारो
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालसहित ५० देशका नागरिकले अब अमेरिकी बी–वान र बी–टु भिजिटर भिसाका लागि अधिकतम २० हजार अमेरिकी डलरसम्म धरौटी राख्नुपर्ने भएको छ । अगस्ट ३ देखि लागू हुने नयाँ व्यवस्थाले भिसा आवेदन प्रक्रिया थप कडा र खर्चिलो बन्ने भएको छ ।

अमेरिका जाने योजना बनाइरहनुभएको छ ? विशेषगरी व्यापार वा घुमघामका लागि बी–वान वा बी–टु भिजिटर भिसा लिने सोचमा हुनुहुन्छ भने अब एउटा ठूलो परिवर्तनबारे तपाईल जान्नै पर्ने भएको छ । अमेरिकी सरकारले भिजिटर भिसामा लागू गर्दै आएको धरौटी प्रणालीलाई अब स्थायी बनाउने निर्णय गरेको छ ।

योसँगै धरौटी रकम पनि उल्लेख्य रूपमा बढाएको छ । अगस्ट ३, २०२६ अर्थात् पर्सी सोमवारदेखि लागू हुने नयाँ नियमअनुसार नेपालसहित तोकिएका ५० देशका बी–वान र बी–टु भिसा आवेदकले अब १० हजार, १५ हजार वा २० हजार अमेरिकी डलरसम्म धरौटी राख्नुपर्नेछ । यसअघि परीक्षण कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत अधिकतम १५ हजार डलरसम्मको व्यवस्था थियो ।

सामान्यतया कन्सुलर अधिकारीले १५ हजार डलर धरौटी निर्धारण गर्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ । तर आवेदकको भ्रमणको उद्देश्य, रोजगारी, आम्दानी र अन्य अवस्थाका आधारमा यो रकम १० हजार वा २० हजार डलरसम्म हुन सक्छ । यो व्यवस्था पहिलो पटक अगस्ट २०२५ मा परीक्षणका रूपमा सुरु गरिएको थियो ।

अमेरिकी विदेश मन्त्रालयका अनुसार एक वर्षको अनुभवले यो प्रणालीले भिसाका शर्त पालना गराउन प्रभावकारी भूमिका खेलेको देखिएको छ । यसो गर्दा उच्च ओभरस्टे दर, कमजोर सूचना आदानप्रदान, पहिचान प्रमाणीकरण र यात्रा कागजातको सुरक्षामा कमजोरी भएका देशमाथि कूटनीतिक दबाब सिर्जना गर्ने उद्देश्य पनि यसमा रहेको मन्त्रालयको भनाइ छ ।

भिसा प्रक्रिया कसरी शुरु हुन्छ ?

सबैभन्दा पहिले अन्य गैरआवासीय भिसा आवेदनजस्तै अन्तर्वार्ताको समय लिनुपर्नेछ र नियमित भिसा शुल्क तिर्नुपर्नेछ । त्यसपछि कन्सुलर अधिकारीले सबै योग्यता पुगेको र तपाईं तोकिएको देशको नागरिक भएको ठहर गरेमा भिसा तत्काल जारी हुँदैन । अध्यागमन तथा राष्ट्रियता ऐनको धारा २२१ जी अन्तर्गत भिसा अस्थायी रूपमा रोक्का गरिन्छ । त्यसपछि गृह सुरक्षा मन्त्रालयको धरौटी फाराम र सरकारी विद्युतीय भुक्तानी प्रणालीमार्फत धरौटी बुझाउन भनिन्छ । यो रकम आवेदक आफैंले वा तेस्रो पक्षले पनि तिर्न सक्नेछन् ।

धरौटी प्राप्त भएपछि अन्तिम समीक्षा हुनेछ । स्वीकृति पाए तीनदेखि १२ महिनासम्म वैध रहने सिंगल वा मल्टिपल इन्ट्री भिसा जारी हुन सक्नेछ । भिसामै धरौटी बुझाइएको विवरण पनि उल्लेख हुनेछ । अमेरिकी विदेश मन्त्रालयका अनुसार यो कार्यक्रमको उद्देश्य रकम उठाउनु मात्रे होइन । एक वर्षको परीक्षणले यात्रुहरूलाई भिसाका शर्त पालना गराउन यो प्रणाली प्रभावकारी देखिएको मन्त्रालयको निष्कर्ष छ ।

त्यस्तै उच्च ओभरस्टे दर, कमजोर सूचना आदानप्रदान, पहिचान प्रमाणीकरण र यात्रा कागजातको सुरक्षामा कमजोरी भएका देशमाथि कूटनीतिक दबाब सिर्जना गर्ने उद्देश्य पनि यसमा रहेको बताइएको छ । यद्यपि धरौटी फिर्ता हुने व्यवस्था पनि छ । त्यसका लागि भिसा बाहकले अनधिकृत रूपमा काम गर्नु हुँदैन, अनुमति अवधिभित्र अमेरिका छाड्नुपर्छ वा आवश्यक परे समयमै बसाइ अवधि थप अथवा भिसा स्टेटस परिवर्तनका लागि आवेदन दिनुपर्छ ।

सरकारी प्रणालीले सबै शर्त पालना भएको पुष्टि गरेपछि धरौटी स्वतः रद्द हुनेछ र पूरा रकम कुनै ब्याजबिना फिर्ता हुनेछ । तर यदि अनुमति अवधिभन्दा बढी अमेरिका बसियो, आवेदन ढिलो गरियो, अस्वीकृतिपछि १० दिनभित्र पनि अमेरिका छाडिएन वा शरण अथवा अन्य मानवीय संरक्षणका लागि आवेदन दिइयो भने धरौटी रकम स्वतः जफत हुन सक्छ । यस्तो अवस्थामा अन्तिम निर्णय भने होमल्याण्ड सेक्युरिटीले गर्नेछ । एउटा रोचक तथ्य के भने परीक्षण कार्यक्रम सुरु गर्दा एक वर्षमा करिब दुई हजार आवेदक मात्रै धरौटीको दायरामा पर्ने अनुमान गरिएको थियो ।

तर वास्तविक संख्या झन्डै २० हजार पुग्यो । तीमध्ये करिब आधाले मात्रै धरौटी बुझाए । त्यसको प्रभाव भिसा जारी हुने दरमै देखियो । कार्यक्रम लागू भएका देशका नागरिकका लागि बी–श्रेणी भिसा जारी हुने दर पहिलो १० महिनामै अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा ८३ प्रतिशतले घटेको अमेरिकी विदेश मन्त्रालयले जनाएको छ ।

यदि तपाईं अमेरिका भ्रमणको तयारीमा हुनुहुन्छ भने पक्कै पनि अब भिसा आवेदनको चेकलिस्टमा एउटा नयाँ कुरा धरौटी थपिएको छ । भिसाका लागि आवेदन दिनुअघि यो नयाँ व्यवस्था बुझ्न एकदमै महत्वपूर्ण छ । त्यसैले आवेदन अघि यी नियमहरू राम्रोसँग बुझेर मात्रै प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढाउनु उपयुक्त हुनेछ ।

articles.title: मलेसिया रोजगारीमा सिण्डिकेटविरूद्द लोकतान्त्रिक एसोसियसन
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । मलेसिया रोजगारीमा एकाधिकार (सिण्डिकेट) लगाउन खोजिएको भन्दै वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायसँग सम्बन्धित विभिन्न संगठनहरूले आन्दोलनको चेतावनी दिएका छन् । नेपाल लोकतान्त्रिक वैदेशिक रोजगार एसोसियसनको आयोजनामा शुक्रबार काठमाडौंमा वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायसँग सम्बन्धित विभिन्न संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूले यस्तो चेतावनी दिएका हुन् ।

एसोसियसनले मलेसिया रोजगारीमा केही व्यवसायीहरूले सिण्डिकेट लगाउन खोजेको भन्दै छलफल आयोजना गरेको महासचिव सुमनराज पाण्डेले बताए । ‘केही व्यवसायीहरूको निहित स्वार्थमा मलेसिया रोजगारीमा सिण्डिकेट लगाउन खोजिएको छ । यो विल्कुल गलत छ,’ महासचिव पाण्डेले भने, आजबाट सरोकारवालाहरूसँग छलफल शुरू भएको छ । सिण्डिकेट लागू भयो भने हामी आन्दोलनमा उत्रन्छौं । एसोसियसनले वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघले सिण्डिकेटविरूद्द पहल नगरे एक्लै भएपनि संघर्षमा उत्रने तयारी गरेको छ ।

छलफलमा एसोसियसनका पूर्वअध्यक्ष प्रज्ञान न्यौपाने, कुमुद खनाल, दीपक थापा, नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघका निवर्तमान अध्यक्ष भुवनसिंह गुरूङ,संघका पूर्वमहासचिव मेघनाथ भुर्तेल, प्रगतिशिल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी मञ्चका उपाध्यक्ष सरिता घले, नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायिक गणतान्त्रिक मञ्चका अध्यक्ष धनलाल जैशी, एकीकृत वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संगठनका कार्यवाहक अध्यक्ष मीन प्रसाद गोलेसहित तामाङ समान, नेवा समाज, मगर समाज, महिला संघलगायत थुप्रै घटक संस्थाहरू सहभागी थिए ।

उनीहरूले व्यवसायीहरूको छाता संस्था वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघको भूमिकामाथि पनि प्रश्न उठाएका छन् । एसोसियसनका कार्यवाहक अध्यक्ष सुवर्ण लामाले सिण्डिकेटविरूद्द संघको ध्यानाकर्षण गराउने बताए ।

articles.title: स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति कौडीमा एनसेलले हात पारेपछि हंगामा, भुपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउपछि चासो बढ्यो
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणका पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका छन्। नेपाल प्रहरीको सीआइबीले भण्डारीलाई अनुसन्धानका लागि पक्राउ गरेको छ। भण्डारी किन पक्राउ परे? स्मार्ट प्रकरणमा भण्डारीको भूमिका के? चासो देखिन्छन्।

नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणका पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका छन्। स्मार्ट सेलको सम्पत्ति बेचेर राज्यलाई हानी नोक्सानी पु¥याएको आरोपमा उनी पक्राउ परेका हुन्। तत्कालीन समयमा रेखा शर्मा सञ्चार तथा सूचना प्रविधिमन्त्री हुँदा भण्डारी विज्ञको रूपमा उनको सचिवालयमा नियुक्त भएका थिए ।

सचिवालयमा विज्ञ भनिएका भण्डारीलाई टेरामक्स प्रकरणले चिठ्ठा नै पर्ने स्थिति बन्यो। त्यसपछि टेरामक्स प्रकरणमा प्राधिकारणका तत्कालीन अध्यक्ष पुरुषोत्तम खनाल भ्रष्टाचार मुद्दाका कारण निलम्बित भएपछि उनले प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष पदमा सहजै पुग्ने स्थिति निर्माण गरे। तर, भण्डारी अध्यक्ष बनेपछि नै स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति कौडीको भाउमा वेच्ने काम भएको बताइन्छ। राज्यको नाममा आईसकेको टेलिकमको सम्पत्तिलाई निजी कम्पनी एनसेललाई कौडीको भाउमा बेच्न सघाएको आरोपमा भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका हुन्।

के भन्यो सीआइबीले ?

नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)ले शुक्रबार ललितपुरको धापाखेलबाट पक्राउ गरेको जनाएको छ। उनलाई स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा अनुसन्धानका लागि पक्राउ गरिएको बताइएको छ। सीआईबीले सरकारको स्वामित्वमा आएको स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति बेइमानीपूर्वक सरकारको हक टुटाउन काम गराएको आरोपमा भण्डारी माथि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको थियो।

दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणबाट आधारभूत टेलिफोन सेवा सञ्चालन गर्न स्मार्ट टेलिकमले २०७० वैशाखमा अनुमति पाएको थियो। तर अनुमतिपत्र नवीकरण नगरेपछि स्मार्ट टेलिकमको लाइसेन्स स्वतः रद्द भएको थियो। यसरी सरकारको नाममा पुगिसकेको सम्पत्तिलाई बेचबिखन गर्नका निम्ति सघाएको आरोप भण्डारीमाथि समेत लागेको छ। प्राधिकरण नियामक निकाय समेत भएकाले पनि उनीमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने माग पहिलेदेखि नै उठ्दै आएको थियो । यता, ब्युरोले वैशाखमा स्मार्ट टेलिकमका तत्कालीन प्रबन्ध निर्देशक सर्वेश जोशीलाई पक्राउ गरिसकेको छ।

स्मार्टमा एनसेलको चलाखी

इजाजत खारेजीपछि विवादास्पद रूपमा सम्पत्ति लिलाम बिक्री भएको स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा निजी क्षेत्रको दूरसञ्चार सेवाप्रदायक कम्पनी एनसेल, त्यहाँका प्रमुख लगानीकर्ता र राजनीतिक नेतृत्वबीच शंकास्पद सम्बन्ध देखिएको भन्दै सीआइबीले अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ।

स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति बिक्रीबाट प्रमुख लाभग्राही एनसेल देखिएको छ। नेपाल दूरसञ्चार नियमावलीको नियम १० क मा एकै कम्पनीले एकभन्दा बढी दूरसञ्चार सेवा प्रदायकको अनुमति नपाउने उल्लेख छ। तर एनसेलमा लगानी गरेकाहरुले नै गैरकानुनीरूपले लिलामी गरिएको स्मार्ट टेलिकममा पनि लगानी सकारेकोे सीआईबीको ठहर छ ।

अहिले अनुसन्धानमा स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सेयर बिक्री, सेयर स्वामित्वको इतिहास, बैंक ऋण, सम्पत्ति हस्तान्तरण र एनसेलसँग जोडिएका विभिन्न कारोबार हेरिएको छ। प्रहरीले स्मार्ट टेलिकम, त्यसका सेयरधनी, सम्पत्ति व्यवस्थापन, उपकरण बिक्री र एनसेलसँग जोडिएका आर्थिक सम्बन्धबारे अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

सीआईबीका अनुसार सम्पत्ति लिलाम प्रक्रियाभन्दा अगाडि नै स्मार्ट टेलिकम र एनसेलबीच सम्बन्ध देखिन्छ। यही आधारमा एनसेलसँग जोडिएका केही उच्च तहका व्यक्तिलाई पनि छानबिनको दायरामा ल्याइएको छ। स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति लिलाम प्रकरणमा एनसेलको नेपालस्थित सञ्चालकहरू सतिशलाल आचार्य, भावना सिंह श्रेष्ठ र सचिनलाल आचार्य पनि अनुसन्धानको राडारमै रहेका छन्।

दुरसञ्चार ऐन र स्वार्थको द्वन्द्ध

दुरसञ्चार ऐन २०५३ को दफा नंवर ३३ को उपदफा १ बमोजिम नेपाल सरकारले स्वामित्वमा आएको सम्पत्ति पूर्व अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिले उपदफा (३) बमोजिम निर्धारण गरिने मूल्य नेपाल सरकारलाई बुझाई पुनः अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त गरी दूरसञ्चार सेवा सञ्चालन गर्न सक्नेछ भनिएको छ ।

फेरि उपदफा २ बमोजिमको मूल्य निर्धारण गर्ने प्रयोजनको लागि नेपाल सरकारले प्राधिकरणको परामर्श लिई बमोजिम विशेषज्ञ व्यक्तिहरुको एक समिति गठन गर्न सक्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको छ । तर, प्राधिकारणले सरकारको स्वामित्वमा आइसकेको स्मार्ट टेलिकम एनसेललाई बेच्ने कुरा नै असंगत, पदीय दुरुपयोग र भ्रष्टाचार हुने दाबीहरु सार्वजनिक भइरहेका छन्।

यस्तो अवस्थामा प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष बनेका भण्डारीले पनि कानूनको उल्लङ्घन गर्दै स्मार्टको पक्षमा काम गरेकाले उनी अनुसन्धानमा तानिएका हुन्। तत्कालीन माओवादी केन्द्रबाट सञ्चारमन्त्री बनेकी शर्माले अध्यक्ष नियुक्त गरेका भण्डारीमाथि पदीय दुरुपयोगको गम्भीर आरोप लाग्दै गर्दा नियुक्ति दिने शर्मामाथि समेत केहिले प्रश्न उठाएका छन्। कतै यो सबै सेटिङमै त भएन?

प्रहरीले अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने बाटो यसतर्फ समेत केन्द्रित गर्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिन थालिएको छ। यद्यपी शर्मामाथि यस्ता आरोप भने सार्वजनिक रुपमा लागेको देखिन्न। तर, सचिवालयको विज्ञ भनिएको कर्मचारीलाई अध्यक्ष नियुक्त गरेपछि कानून मिचेको देखिदा उनीमाथि समेत यस्तो प्रश्न स्वभाविक बन्न पुगेको छ ।

articles.title: ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुप नेपाल प्रवेश : जेम होम कलेक्सन आधिकारिक वितरक नियुक्त
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं। भारतको अग्रणी होम टेक्सटाइल कम्पनी ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपले नेपाली बजारमा औपचारिक रूपमा प्रवेश गरेको छ। कम्पनीले नेपालका लागि आफ्ना होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरूको एकमात्र आधिकारिक वितरकको रूपमा जेम होम कलेक्सन प्राइभेट लिमिटेडलाई नियुक्त गरेको घोषणा गरेको छ। यस सहकार्यसँगै नेपाली उपभोक्ताहरूले अब ट्राइडेन्टका प्रिमियम बेड लिनेन, बाथ लिनेन, तौलियालगायतका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरू आधिकारिक तथा भरपर्दो माध्यमबाट प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन्।

यसअघि नेपाली बजारमा ट्राइडेन्टका उत्पादनहरू प्रायः अनौपचारिक माध्यमबाट भित्रिने गरेकोमा यस नियुक्तिपछि गुणस्तर र प्रामाणिकताको सुनिश्चितता हुने कम्पनीहरूको दाबी छ। यस साझेदारीले नेपालमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रियस्तरका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरूको पहुँच विस्तार गर्ने र नेपाली ग्राहकहरूलाई विश्वस्तरीय गुणस्तर, आधिकारिक आपूर्ति शृंखला तथा उत्कृष्ट ग्राहक सेवा उपलब्ध गराउने लक्ष्य राखेको छ।

जेम होम कलेक्सन प्राइभेट लिमिटेड विगत ३० वर्षदेखि नेपालको फ्लोरिङ तथा फर्निसिङ क्षेत्रमा सक्रिय रहेको कम्पनी हो। यसले आतिथ्य र खुद्रा दुवै बजारका लागि विविध गुणस्तरीय उत्पादनहरू निरन्तर आपूर्ति गर्दै आएको छ। यही दीर्घकालीन बजार अनुभव र स्थापित वितरण सञ्जालका कारण कम्पनीलाई ट्राइडेन्टको आधिकारिक साझेदारका रूपमा छनोट गरिएको बताइएको छ।

ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपको स्थापना सन् १९९० मा भारतीय उद्यमी पद्मश्री राजिन्दर गुप्ताले पञ्जाबबाट सुरु गरेका थिए। सुरुमा एउटा मात्र धागो उत्पादन एकाइबाट सुरु भएको यो समूह हाल विश्वकै सबैभन्दा ठूला टेरी तौलिया उत्पादक र समग्र होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादकहरूमध्ये एक बनेको आर्थिक हिसाबले हेर्ने हो भने पछिल्लो प्रतिवेदन अनुसार ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपले आर्थिक वर्ष २०२६ मा ६५ अर्ब २१ करोड भारतीय रुपैयाँ बराबरको आम्दानी हासिल गरेको थियो, जुन अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा सामान्य घटेको भए पनि खुद नाफा भने बढेको थियो।

चालु आर्थिक वर्षको हालसालैको प्रगति हेर्दा पनि, पहिलो त्रैमासमा आम्दानी १ हजार ८ सय ३० करोड रुपैयाँ पुगेको र खुद नाफा ५५ प्रतिशतले वृद्धि भएको देखिन्छ। कम्पनीको समग्र आकारका सन्दर्भमा हेर्दा, ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुप इन्डियामा हाल १६ हजार ३ सय तीनजना कर्मचारी कार्यरत रहेका छन् र यसको बजार पूँजीकरण करिब १।३२ बिलियन डलर बराबर रहेको पाइन्छ। समूह लामो समयदेखि आफूलाई एक बिलियन डलरभन्दा बढी मूल्यको वैश्विक व्यापारिक समूहको रूपमा चिनाउँदै आएको छ, जसको होम टेक्सटाइल, कागज र रसायन क्षेत्रमा सशक्त उपस्थिति रहेको दाबी गरिन्छ।

यसआधिकारिक वितरण सम्झौतापछि नेपाली उपभोक्ताहरूले अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरू प्रामाणिकताको सुनिश्चितताका साथ प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन् भने होटल तथा रिसोर्ट जस्ता आतिथ्य व्यवसायहरूले पनि विश्वसनीय आपूर्ति स्रोत भेट्टाउने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ। साथै यसले नेपालको होम फर्निसिङ बजारमा स्वस्थ प्रतिस्पर्धा र गुणस्तर सुधारमा समेत योगदान पुर्‍याउने कम्पनीको भनाइ छ।

articles.title: मेची राजमार्ग ठप्प ! सडक बन्द हुँदा बिरामीदेखि ढुवानीसम्म संकट
articles.summary:
इलाम । मेची राजमार्ग अन्तर्गत इलाम माइखोला राजदुवालीकमाथि सडक अवरुद्ध भएको तीन सात भयो । सडक खुल्ने अझै छाँटकाँट छैन । सडक बन्द भएपछि इलाम मात्र हैन पुर्वी पहाडी जिल्ला पाँचथर ताप्लेजुङ लगायतका स्थानीयलाई समेत सास्ती भएको छ ।

मेची राजमार्ग अन्तर्गत इलामको माइखोला (राजदुवाली) माथिको सडक भासिएर तीन सातादेखि अवरुद्ध हुँदा इलामसँगै पाँचथर र ताप्लेजुङका नागरिकले सास्ती भोगिरहेका छन् । सडक बन्द भएपछि सवारी साधन वारिपारि नै रोकिने गरेका छन् भने यात्रुहरू करिब एक किलोमिटर भिरको बाटो पैदल हिँड्न बाध्य छन् ।

बिरामीलाई जनपथ प्रहरी, सशस्त्र प्रहरी र नेपाली सेनाले स्टे«चरमार्फत वारपार गराइरहेका छन् भने एम्बुलेन्स पनि दुवैतर्फबाट सेवा दिन बाध्य छन् । अत्यावश्यक खाद्यान्न, ग्यास र तरकारी ढुवानीसमेत प्रभावित बनेको छ । इलाम नगरपालिकाले सरोकारवाला निकायसँग छलफल गरी पुनः इलामलाई संकटग्रस्त क्षेत्र घोषणा गर्न सरकारसँग माग गरेको छ ।

राजदुवाली खण्डको पहिरो नियन्त्रण, ट्रस्ट पुल मर्मत तथा जोरकलश–हर्कटे सडक स्तरोन्नतिको लागि २४ करोड ९३ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढीको ठेक्का जे एन्ड जे निर्माण सेवा प्रालिले २०८४ असारसम्म सम्पन्न गर्ने गरी लिएको भएपनि हालसम्म समग्रमा १८–२० प्रतिशत मात्र काम भएको सडक डिभिजन कार्यालयले जनाएको छ । स्थानीयले मुख्य सडकभन्दा वैकल्पिक सडक तत्काल सञ्चालनमा ल्याउन माग गरेका छन् ।

गत वर्ष तीन महिनासम्म संकटग्रस्त क्षेत्र घोषणा गरिए पनि प्रभावकारी काम नभएको भन्दै स्थानीय आक्रोशित छन् । सरकारले सडक बनाउन नसके इलामेली आफैंले श्रमदान र चन्दा उठाएर सडक तथा पुल निर्माण गर्ने चेतावनी दिएका छन् ।

सडक अवरुद्धकै कारण बिरामीले समयमै उपचार नपाएर ज्यान गुमाउनुपर्ने अवस्था रहेको भन्दै तत्काल समाधानको माग गरिएको छ ।

उता वैकल्पिक सडकका रूपमा प्रयोग गरिने सिमलगोलाई–तिल्केनी तथा केचना–कञ्चनजंघा सडकको बेलासी–भन्ज्याङ खण्ड पनि निर्माणमा ढिलाइका कारण सञ्चालन योग्य छैन । माइजोगमाई र पुवा खोलाका पुल गत वर्षको बाढीले बगाएपछि अहिलेसम्म पुनर्निर्माण हुन सकेको छैन । यस वर्ष बजेटमै इलामलाई बेवास्ता गरिएको भन्दै स्थानीयले सरकारसँग तत्काल सडक सञ्चालनको सुनिश्चितता गर्न माग गरेका छन् ।

articles.title: बौद्धनाथमा अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिमा राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेप, कसले रोक्यो सम्पूर्णकुमार लामाको नियुक्ति पत्र ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समिति तीन महिनादेखि अध्यक्षविहीन छ । संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्रालय मातहतको यो महत्वपूर्ण निकायमा मन्त्रिपरिषद्बाट अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिको सिफारिस भइसके पनि राजनीतिक स्वार्थका कारण नियुक्तिले अझै पूर्णता पाउन सकेको छैन । अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिको निर्णय भइसकेको एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि नियुक्तिपत्र रोकिँदा सरकारको नियतमाथि नै प्रश्न उठ्न थालेको छ ।

गत असार १८ गते मन्त्रिपरिषद्को निर्णयअनुसार संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्रालयले बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिको अध्यक्षमा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामालाई नियुक्त गर्ने निर्णय गरेको थियो । तर विडम्बना, निर्णय भएको यति समय बितिसक्दा पनि लामाले नियुक्तिपत्र पाएका छैनन् ।

समितिका अध्यक्षसहित पाँच पदाधिकारी नियुक्त गरिए पनि अध्यक्ष लामाबाहेक सबै सदस्यले नियुक्तिपत्र बुझिसकेका छन् । अध्यक्षलाई मात्रै रोक्नुको कारण काठमाडौं–३ का रास्वपा सांसद राजुनाथ पाण्डे रहेको आरोप छ ।

स्थानीयका अनुसार सांसद पाण्डेले आफ्ना निकट व्यक्तिलाई अध्यक्ष बनाउन दबाब दिएपछि लामाको नियुक्तिपत्र रोकिएको हो । लामो समयदेखि समिति नेतृत्वविहीन हुँदा गुठियारदेखि स्थानीय सरोकारवालासम्म सरकारसँग जवाफ माग्न थालेका छन् । उनीहरूको चेतावनी छ, ‘रास्वपाभित्रको जुंगाको लडाइँको छायाँ बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिमा पार्न मिल्दैन ।’

दुई कार्यकाल सफलतापूर्वक अध्यक्षको जिम्मेवारी सम्हालिसकेका सम्पूर्णकुमार लामाको पुनः नियुक्तिका लागि गुठियार, स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधि, विभिन्न संघसंस्था र बुद्धिजीवीहरूले एकमत सिफारिस गरेका थिए । स्थानीयका अनुसार लामा सबैले स्वीकार गरेका र समन्वयकारी क्षमता भएका व्यक्ति हुन् । अध्यक्ष नहुँदा बौद्धनाथमा प्रशासनिक कामदेखि सामाजिक, धार्मिक, सांस्कृतिक तथा विकास निर्माणका गतिविधि प्रभावित भएका छन् । बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिले यहाँका विभिन्न धार्मिक तथा सामाजिक संघसंस्थाबीच समन्वय गर्दै आएको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका पनि अहिले नेतृत्व अभावकै कारण कमजोर बनेको छ ।

अलमलमा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामा

अध्यक्षमा नियुक्ति भइसकेको एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि नियुक्तिपत्र नपाउँदा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामा अन्योलमा परेका छन् । नियुक्ति भइसकेको व्यक्तिलाई नै बदर गराएर अर्को व्यक्तिलाई ल्याउने प्रयास सांसद पाण्डेले गरिरहेको स्थानीयको आरोप छ ।

उनीहरू भन्छन्, ‘सर्वस्वीकार्य व्यक्तिको नियुक्ति रोक्नु सरकारकै लागि ‘ब्याकफायर’ हुन सक्छ ।’ यसअघि पनि सरकार विभिन्न नियुक्ति र निर्णयका कारण विवादमा परिसकेको छ । धार्मिक तथा सांस्कृतिक संस्थामा राजनीतिक भागबन्डा होइन, योग्य र सबैले स्वीकार गर्ने व्यक्तिलाई नेतृत्व दिनुपर्ने स्थानीयको जोड छ । यही विषयलाई लिएर काठमाडौं–३ का सांसद राजुनाथ पाण्डे र संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्री खडकराज पौडेल ९गणेश० बीच पनि मतभेद उत्पन्न भएको बताइएको छ ।

समितिका पाँच सदस्यमा विशाल लामा, निर्भिक्ता थिङ लामा, सेनाङ ग्याम्जो तामाङ, रोशनकुमार श्रेष्ठ र मणिभद्र पोखरेल नियुक्त भइसकेका छन् । तर अध्यक्षको नियुक्तिपत्र अझै रोकिँदा बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समिति नेतृत्वविहीन अवस्थामै अल्झिएको छ र राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेपको आरोप झन् गहिरिँदै गएको छ ।

articles.title: पूजारी भन्छन्– बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको भ्रमले दर्शनार्थी घटे
articles.summary:
म्याग्दी । म्याग्दीको बेनी नगरपालिका ९ स्थित देशकै ऐतिहासिक र धार्मिक महत्व बोकेको गलेश्वरधाममा यस वर्षको साउन महिनामा विगतका वर्षको तुलनामा भक्तजनको चहलपहलमा कमि आएको छ ।

बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको अवधिमा शुभकार्य गर्न नहुने धार्मिक मान्यताका कारण पनि दर्शनार्थीहरुको कमी आएको हो ।

साउन महिना भगवान शिवको अत्यन्त प्रिय महिना भएकाले यस अवधिमा शिवको आराधना, रुद्राभिषेक, बेलपत्र चढाउने तथा जल चढाउनु विशेष फलदायी मानिन्छ । तर बृहस्पति अन्ध भएकै कारण मन्दिरमा दर्शन गर्न हुँदैन भन्ने भ्रम फैलिएको छ ।

बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको अवधिमा शुभकार्य गर्न नहुने धार्मिक मान्यतालाई लिएर दर्शनसमेत गर्न नहुने भन्ने भ्रमका कारण भक्तजनको संख्या घटेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालयका गलेश्वरधामका मूल पुजारी चन्द्रमणि आचार्यका अनुसार धार्मिक शास्त्रमा भगवानको दर्शन र पूजा–अर्चना गर्न कुनै निषेध गरिएको छैन । बरु साउन महिनामा शिवको आराधना गर्दा विशेष पुण्य प्राप्त हुने धार्मिक विश्वास छ ।

गलेश्वरधाममा रहेको प्राकृतिक शिलामाथि अवस्थित स्वयं प्रकट शिवलिङ्ग विशेष आकर्षणको केन्द्र हो । एउटै ९ रोपनी क्षेत्रफलको विशाल चट्टानमाथि रहेको यो शिवलिङ्ग देश–विदेशका भक्तजनका लागि श्रद्धाको केन्द्र बनेको छ ।

विशेषगरी साउन महिना, महाशिवरात्रि, बालाचतुर्दशी तथा तीजका अवसरमा यहाँ हजारौँ श्रद्धालुको भीड लाग्ने गर्दछ ।

धेरै धार्मिक स्थलहरुमा पछि स्थापना गरिएको शिवलिङ्गमा पुजा गरिन्छ भने गलेश्वरधाममा स्वयं उत्पत्ती ज्योतिर्लिङ्ग भएको हुँदा पनि यस स्थानको छुट्टै धार्मिक महत्व हुने बताइन्छ ।

साउनको दोस्रो सोमबार भक्तजनले चढाएको भेटी गणना गरी बेनीस्थित गरिमा विकास बैंकमा दाखिला गरिएको छ । पहिलो सोमबार करिब दुई लाख रुपैयाँ भेटी संकलन भएको गलेश्वरधाममा दोस्रो सोमबार पनि करिब सोही हाराहारी रकम संकलन भएको थियो । भक्तजनको संख्या केही घटे पनि धार्मिक आस्थाका साथ दर्शन गर्ने क्रम भने निरन्तर भइरहेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालय क्षेत्र परिसरमा निर्माण गरिएको १०८ शिवलिङ्ग भक्तजनका लागि अर्को प्रमुख आकर्षण बनेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालय क्षेत्र विकास कोषका उपाध्यक्ष बमबहादुर पुनको अगुवाइमा चन्दा तथा सहयोगबाट संकलित करिब साढे १३ लाख रुपैयाँमध्ये साढे ७ लाख रुपैयाँ खर्च गरेर शिवलिङ्ग निर्माण गरिएको थियो ।

२०७६ सालमा निर्माण गरीएको यो धार्मिक महत्व दिने आकृति एकै स्थानमा १०८ शिवलिङ्गको दर्शन र पूजा गर्न सकिने भएपछि दैनिक रूपमा भक्तजन पुग्ने गरेका छन् ।

धार्मिक, सांस्कृतिक र प्राकृतिक सम्पदाको अनुपम संगमका रूपमा रहेको गलेश्वरधामले म्याग्दीको धार्मिक पर्यटन प्रवद्र्धनमा समेत महत्वपूर्ण योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ । २०८२ सालका चार वटा सोमबार गरी झण्डै १७ लाख रुपियाँ भेटी संकलन भएको थियो ।

articles.title: बैतेश्वर गाउँपालिकामा भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सेवा शुरु
articles.summary:
दोलखा । नेपालको संविधानले स्थानीय तहबाटै भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सेवा प्रवाह गर्ने व्यवस्था गरेको ११ वर्षपछि दोलखाको बैतेश्वर गाउँपालिकाले जिल्लामै पहिलो पटक भूमि व्यवस्थापन शाखामार्फत मालपोत र नापीसम्बन्धी सेवा सञ्चालनमा ल्याएको छ ।

अब नागरिकले आफ्नै पालिकाबाट भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सेवा पाउने भएका छन् । २०७२ सालको संविधानले स्थानीय तहलाई भूमिसम्बन्धी सेवा प्रवाह गर्ने अधिकार दिएको थियो ।

त्यसलाई कार्यान्वयन गर्न नेपाल सरकारको भूमि व्यवस्था, सहकारी तथा गरिबी निवारण मन्त्रालय तथा संघीय मामिला तथा सामान्य प्रशासन मन्त्रालयले इच्छुक स्थानीय तहबाट आवेदन माग गरेपछि बैतेश्वर गाउँपालिका छनोटमा परेको हो ।

आवश्यक तयारी पूरा गरेपछि भूमि प्रशासन कार्यालय दोलखाले सेवा हस्तान्तरण गरेको छ । भूमि व्यवस्थापन शाखा सञ्चालनसँगै जग्गा किनबेच, नामसारी, अंशबण्डा, दानपत्र, हकछोड, सट्टापट्टा, नक्सा प्रिन्ट, कित्ता रेखाङ्कन लगायतका विभिन्न सेवा चरणबद्ध रूपमा गाउँपालिकाबाटै उपलब्ध हुने जनाइएको छ ।

सेवा लिन चाहने नागरिकमध्ये डिजिटल प्रणालीमा आबद्ध भइसकेकाले पालिकाबाटै सेवा लिन सक्नेछन्। डिजिटल प्रणालीमा आबद्ध नभएकाले भने पहिलो पटक भूमि प्रशासन कार्यालयमा गई आफ्नो अभिलेख डिजिटल प्रणालीमा दर्ता गराउनुपर्नेछ ।

नयाँ प्रणाली लागू भएसँगै सेवा नागरिकको घरदैलोमा पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिए पनि केही प्राविधिक चुनौती भने बाँकी नै छन् । भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सम्पूर्ण अभिलेख डिजिटल प्रणालीमा आधारित भएकाले श्रेस्ता (मूल अभिलेख) गाउँपालिकामा नहुँदा केही कानुनी तथा प्राविधिक जटिलता आउन सक्ने बताइएको छ । स्थानीय तहबाटै सेवा उपलब्ध हुन थालेपछि नागरिकको समय, खर्च र सदरमुकाम चरिकोट धाउनुपर्ने बाध्यता कम हुने भन्दै स्थानीय भने खुसी देखिन्छन् ।

संविधानले परिकल्पना गरेको स्थानीय तहबाट भूमि प्रशासन सेवा प्रवाहको व्यवस्था दोलखामा पनि कार्यान्वयनमा आएको हो । यसको प्रभावकारिता भने सेवा प्रवाहको गुणस्तर, डिजिटल प्रणालीको विश्वसनीयता र बाँकी प्राविधिक चुनौती समाधानमा निर्भर रहनेछ ।

articles.title: बुद्धकै पालादेखि शुरु भएको वर्षावास, किन शुरु भयो यस्तो परम्परा ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । असार पूर्णिमासँगै बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीहरूको तीन महिने वर्षावास सुरु भएको छ । गौतम बुद्धकै समयदेखि चल्दै आएको २५ सय वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आत्मअनुशासन, ध्यान, साधना र आध्यात्मिक उन्नतिको प्रतीक मानिन्छ । बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीहरूको अत्यन्तै महत्वपूर्ण धार्मिक परम्परा तीन महिने वर्षावास शुरु भएको छ । हरेक वर्ष असार पूर्णिमादेखि कार्तिक पूर्णिमासम्म चल्ने यो परम्परा भिक्षुहरू एकै ठाउँमा बस्ने अभ्यास मात्रै होइन, यो अनुशासन, ध्यान, आध्यात्मिक साधना र बुद्धको जीवनसँग प्रत्यक्ष जोडिएको ऐतिहासिक अभ्यास पनि हो । बुद्धकै समयदेखि सुरु भएको यो परम्परा आखिर २५ सय वर्षपछि पनि किन उस्तै सान्दर्भिक छ ?

वर्षावासको सुरुवात

बुद्धले आफ्ना भिक्षुहरूलाई एउटा महत्वपूर्ण निर्देशन दिनुभएको थियो, “चरथ भिक्खवे चारिकं बहुजन हिताय, बहुजन सुखाय ।’ अर्थात्, “हे भिक्षुहरू ! बहुजनको हित र सुखका लागि गाउँ–गाउँ, नगर–नगर जाऊ, धर्म प्रचार गर ।’ बुद्धत्व प्राप्त गरेपछि भिक्षुहरू वर्षभरि विभिन्न स्थानमा धर्म प्रचार गर्न जान्थे । तर वर्षायाम सुरु भएपछि यात्रा कठिन हुन्थ्यो । बाटो बिग्रिन्थ्यो ।

नदीहरू बढ्थे । जीवजन्तु र बोटबिरुवामा क्षति पुग्ने सम्भावना पनि हुन्थ्यो । यही कारणले बुद्धले वर्षाको तीन महिना एकै स्थानमा बसेर ध्यान, अध्ययन र साधना गर्न निर्देशन दिनुभयो ।

यही अभ्यास नै पछि वर्षावासका रूपमा स्थापित भयो । धेरैलाई थाहा नहुन सक्छ, बौद्ध ग्रन्थमा उल्लेख भए अनुसार भगवान बुद्धले आफ्नो जीवनकालमा ४५ पटक वर्षावास बिताउनुभएको उल्लेख पाइन्छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष वर्षायाममा उहाँ कुनै न कुनै विहार, वन वा उपासकले बनाइदिएको आरामस्थलमा बस्नुहुन्थ्यो । यसले देखाउँछ, बुद्धले केवल उपदेश मात्र दिनुभएन । आफूले सिकाएको अभ्यासलाई जीवनभर पालना पनि गर्नुभयो ।

वर्षातको समयमा प्राकृतिक विपतिहरुबाट जोगिन र जोगाउनका साथै एकै ठाउँमा बसी नियमपुर्वक धार्मिक किसिमले जिवनयापन गर्नु नै यसको मुख्य उद्देश्य हो ।

वर्षावास किन विशेष छ ?

वर्षावास भिक्षुहरूको बसाइ मात्रै होइन । यो आत्मअनुशासनको समय हो । यस अवधिमा भिक्षुहरूले गहिरो ध्यान, विनयको अध्ययन, धर्म छलफल र आध्यात्मिक अभ्यासलाई प्राथमिकता दिन्छन् । उता गृहस्थ उपासक–उपासिकाहरू पनि विहारमा पुगेर दान, शील, ध्यान र धर्मश्रवणमार्फत आफ्नो आध्यात्मिक जीवनलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाउने प्रयास गर्छन् ।

वर्षावासपछि आउने कथिना चिवरदान

वर्षावास सकिएपछि बौद्ध समाजमा अर्को महत्वपूर्ण परम्परा सुरु हुन्छ कथिन चिवरदान । तीन महिना अनुशासित जीवन बिताएका भिक्षुहरूलाई श्रद्धालुहरूले सामूहिक रूपमा चिवर अर्पण गर्छन् । बौद्ध परम्परामा यसलाई सबैभन्दा ठूलो सामूहिक दानमध्ये एक मानिन्छ । यसले भिक्षु र गृहस्थबीचको सम्बन्धलाई अझ मजबुत बनाउने विश्वास गरिन्छ ।

बाइट–भिक्षु कौन्डण्य, विहार प्रमुख, बुद्ध विहार

विशेषगरी यो समयमा बौद्धमार्गीहरु विभिन्न विहारमा गई बुद्ध, धर्म, संघको गुणानुस्मरण गरी ध्यान भावना गरी आध्यात्मिक उन्नती तर्फ अग्रसर हुने गर्दछन् । विशेषगरी थेरवाद बुद्धधर्मको प्रभाव रहेको मुलुकमा वर्षावास परम्पराले धार्मिक आध्यात्मिक क्षेत्रमा सकारात्मक प्रभाव पारेको कारणले यसलाई बुद्धकालिन समयदेखि अहिलेसम्म पनि निरन्तरता दिइरहेको छ ।

२५ सय वर्षदेखि नटुटेको परम्परा

विश्वका धेरै धार्मिक अभ्यास समयसँगै परिवर्तन भएका छन् । तर वर्षावास भने बुद्धकालदेखि आजसम्म मूल स्वरूपमै कायम छ । नेपाल, श्रीलंका, थाइल्याण्ड, म्यानमार, कम्बोडिया, लाओस लगायत थेरवाद बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बी देशहरूमा आज पनि लाखौं भिक्षुहरू वर्षायाममा एकै स्थानमा बसेर यही परम्परा निर्वाह गर्छन् । समय फेरियो । प्रविधि फेरियो, समाज फेरियो । तर ध्यान, अनुशासन र आत्मशुद्धिको मूल्य कहिल्यै फेरिएन । सायद यही कारणले वर्षावास आज पनि उत्तिकै जीवित र सान्दर्भिक बनेको छ । बुद्धले सुरु गर्नुभएको वर्षावास अहिले एउटा धार्मिक अनुष्ठानमा मात्रै सिमित छैन ।

यो आत्मसंयम, करुणा, अनुशासन र आध्यात्मिक विकासको तीन महिने यात्राको रुपमा समेत स्थापित भइसकेको छ । बुद्धकै पालादेखि सुरु भएको यो परम्पराले आज पनि संसारभरका लाखौं बौद्ध अनुयायीलाई ध्यान, धर्म र आत्मपरिवर्तनतर्फ प्रेरित गरिरहेको छ ।

articles.title: घरभाडा व्यवस्थापन अब डिजिटल : घरधनी र भाडावालाको झन्झट अन्त्य गर्न ‘भाडासेवा’ बजारमा
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालमा घर, फ्ल्याट, सटर तथा व्यावसायिक भवनको व्यवस्थापनलाई डिजिटल बनाउने उद्देश्यले एजिनेक्स क्लाउडले ‘भाडासेवा’ नामक क्लाउड–आधारित प्रणाली सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। ‘व्यवस्थित र सुमधुर सम्बन्धका लागि भाडासेवा’ मूल नारासहित आएको यो प्रणालीले कागजी अभिलेख र एक्सेल फाइलको झन्झट अन्त्य गर्दै घरभाडा व्यवस्थापनका सम्पूर्ण प्रक्रियालाई एकै डिजिटल प्लेटफर्ममा समेटेको छ।

यस प्रणालीमार्फत प्रयोगकर्ताले भवन तथा कोठाहरुको रियल–टाइम अनुगमन, भाडावालाको डिजिटल प्रोफाइल, अनलाइन सम्झौता र डिजिटल हस्ताक्षर गर्न सक्नेछन्। साथै, मासिक भाडा र बिजुली–पानीको बिल स्वतः तयार हुने, अनलाइन भुक्तानी गर्न मिल्ने तथा स्वचालित रसिद आउने सुविधा यसमा रहेको छ।

अपार्टमेन्ट तथा व्यावसायिक कम्प्लेक्सका साझा खर्च (CAM) व्यवस्थापन, मर्मतसम्भार ट्र्याकिङ, कर्मचारी व्यवस्थापन र आम्दानी–खर्चको विस्तृत रिपोर्टिङसमेत यसैबाट गर्न सकिन्छ।

साना घरधनीदेखि ठूला सपिङ मल र व्यावसायिक कम्प्लेक्ससम्मका लागि उपयोगी यो प्रणाली कम्प्युटर, ट्याब्लेट र मोबाइलबाटै सजिलै चलाउन सकिन्छ।

articles.title: Financial constraints fueling informal women’s labour migration to Kuwait
articles.summary:
Nearly 69,000 Nepalis are employed as domestic workers in Kuwait despite a government ban on sending workers for such jobs, proof that Nepal’s migration policy is increasingly out of step with the economic realities driving women to seek work abroad.

The figures, provided by Kuwait’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs to the Embassy of Nepal in Kuwait, expose the widening gap between government policy and the reality of overseas employment. They also show how restrictions introduced to protect vulnerable workers have failed to prevent migration and have instead pushed many aspiring workers towards informal recruitment channels.

The ban originated from a directive issued on April 2, 2017 by parliament’s International Relations and Labour Committee. The committee instructed the cabinet to stop sending domestic workers to Gulf countries until destination countries introduced protective laws and signed bilateral labour agreements with Nepal.

Following the directive, legal departures for domestic employment came to a halt.

However, official figures show that thousands of Nepalis have continued to work as domestic workers in Kuwait.

According to the diplomatic communication received by the embassy, Kuwait is home to 186,000 Nepali nationals. Of them, 115,000 work in the private sector, 421 in the public sector and 68,900 as domestic staff in private households.

Nepalis now account for around four percent of Kuwait’s total population.

Statistics released on June 30 by Kuwait’s Public Authority for Civil Information show that the country hosts more than 2.8 million foreign workers, including 883,308 domestic workers.

For many Nepali women, the ban has not removed the need to seek employment abroad. Instead, financial pressures have pushed many to rely on informal channels to reach countries where domestic work is in demand.

Sunita Limbu, a domestic worker in Kuwait, said economic hardship forced her to seek employment despite the restrictions.

“I have a five-year-old son and a chronically ill husband,” Limbu told Kantipur. “I need to pay for my son’s education and husband’s treatment. I earn Rs50,000 a month here, but I had to come through unauthorised routes. Had we been allowed to migrate legally, we could at least visit our families during scheduled leave.”

Recruitment networks operating in both Nepal and Kuwait have filled the gap created by the absence of legal channels. In Kuwait, the domestic worker recruitment system is formally regulated. The Public Authority for Manpower (PAM) issues licences to agencies that recruit domestic workers and supply them to employers.

By 2025, as many as 488 manpower agencies held valid licences from PAM. A Kuwaiti employer can pay up to 1,500 Kuwaiti dinars, equivalent to around Rs750,000, to a licensed local agency to hire a domestic worker. Such payments create incentives for recruitment networks in Nepal to identify and send workers through informal arrangements.

Labour migration expert Saru Joshi Shrestha said restrictions alone cannot prevent people from seeking employment abroad when economic opportunities at home remain limited.

“Unless the state guarantees sustainable domestic employment, no administrative prohibition can stop women from seeking livelihoods abroad,” Shrestha said. “When legal avenues are shut down without creating jobs at home, people inevitably find informal routes. The government must regulate the sector rather than enforce ineffective bans.”

A government task force led by Ram Kaji Khadka, head of the Central, West Asia, and Africa Division at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, reached a similar conclusion.

In a report submitted to the foreign and labour ministries, the task force said preventing unskilled or economically vulnerable people from taking up domestic work abroad had diverted them towards networks that arrange travel through visit visas.

The report said most domestic workers come from economically disadvantaged families and include many single mothers. It identified Jhapa, Sindhupalchok, Makawanpur, Morang, Kathmandu, Kavre, Ilam, Nuwakot, Sunsari and Chitwan as major districts of origin.

The report concluded that the ban had increased workers’ vulnerability by limiting their access to social security, emergency assistance and legal protection.

Former Nepali ambassador to Kuwait Madhuban Paudel said the government’s approach had failed to address the underlying challenges faced by domestic workers.

“Those who raise this issue in parliament do not understand the core reality of domestic workers’ plight,” Paudel said. “The state must either enforce a total physical restriction on departures, which is impossible, or regulate the process. Imposing a ban while allowing human trafficking to thrive is no solution.”

Paudel said the policy had also complicated Nepal’s diplomatic engagement with destination countries.

“Destination governments become aggrieved when Nepal labels these workers ‘illegal’ simply because they lacked Nepali labour permits,” he said. “In their eyes, holding a valid passport and visa makes a worker legitimate under domestic law. They maintain that Nepal cannot brand workers illegal once they arrive on their soil.”

The government has also acknowledged that the restrictions have not stopped women from travelling to the Gulf for domestic work.

On May 8, 2025, Foreign Secretary Amrit Kumar Rai informed parliament’s Industry, Commerce, Labour and Consumer Interest Committee that large numbers of Nepali women continue to reach Gulf countries as domestic workers through informal channels despite the existing restrictions.

Nepal has attempted to address the issue by negotiating a bilateral labour agreement with Kuwait that would establish a regulated pathway for domestic workers.

Pitambar Ghimire, spokesperson for the Ministry of Labour, said discussions with Kuwait are ongoing.

“Signing a bilateral labour agreement with Kuwait is a priority for the government,” Ghimire said. “Drafts have been diplomatically exchanged, but we have yet to reach a final consensus.”

However, progress has been slow, partly because of strict conditions set by parliament before domestic workers can be sent abroad again.

On September 29, 2020, the parliamentary committee issued a seven-point directive requiring destination countries to provide separate legal protections for domestic workers.

The conditions include guarantees on minimum wages, weekly and annual leave, social security, occupational safety, 24-hour insurance coverage, overtime payments, dispute resolution mechanisms, pre-departure and post-arrival training, protection against discrimination and strict penalties for abuse by employers.

Nepal has shared draft agreements based on these requirements with Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Qatar. However, foreign ministry officials say destination countries have shown limited urgency in signing binding agreements as recruitment networks continue supplying workers through informal channels.

Meanwhile, the Embassy of Nepal in Kuwait faces difficulties assisting workers who arrive outside formal labour migration systems.

Nepali Ambassador to Kuwait Ghanshyam Lamsal said the absence of official records makes it harder for the embassy to provide legal support, insurance assistance and emergency rescue services.

“We have clearly communicated the ground realities and diplomatic complexities to relevant government bodies in Kathmandu,” Lamsal said. “Rescuing workers who arrive through illegal channels poses enormous hurdles.”

The ambassador declined to comment directly on the parliamentary ban.

articles.title: Ignored safety rules drive up deadly accidents in Phewa Lake
articles.summary:
On June 23, 19-year-old Amar Thapa from Ram Bazar, Pokhara, went to Phewa Lake to try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP), a water sport that has rapidly caught the attention of the city’s youth.

Thapa paddled into the lake after 6 pm. Within less than an hour, the outing turned fatal. At around 6:40 pm, he fell into the water and disappeared.

A disaster management team from the Armed Police Force, Pokhara, including trained deep-water divers, recovered his body at around 9:10 pm from a depth of about 25 feet. Police detained the lifeguard working for the paddleboard operator immediately after the incident and arrested the company owner the following day. Both were charged with causing death through business negligence and have since been released on bail.

Thapa’s death was not an isolated tragedy. Eight people lost their lives in Phewa Lake in the last fiscal year alone, according to records maintained by security agencies.

The deaths expose a growing safety crisis in one of Nepal’s most popular tourist destinations, where new recreational activities have expanded faster than regulations and enforcement mechanisms.

On February 14, 24-year-old Adit Gurung died after his car veered off the road near Gaira Chautara and plunged into the lake. On April 10, 32-year-old Nisu Bhagat (Agarwal), a resident of Siliguri, India, drowned while swimming. On May 1, 10-year-old Aarish Lama from Khapaudi died while swimming in the lake. Weeks later, on May 21, 27-year-old Riwaj Gurung from Kahun Khola, in Pokhara, also drowned while swimming.

The fatalities continued into June. A day after Thapa died on a stand-up paddleboard, 34-year-old Shankar Nepali from Nayabazar drowned at around 5:30 pm while fishing near Khapaundi.

Concerned by the rising number of incidents, the District Administration Office (DAO) issued a safety notice on June 25 along with stricter rules for boats, kayaks and surfing equipment operating on the lake.

The notice required all water sports operators to register their businesses, provide life jackets to customers, maintain safety insurance coverage, follow designated operating hours and monitor weather conditions before allowing activities. The administration also warned of legal action against businesses that ignored the rules.

But the directives have done little to prevent further deaths.

On July 10, 36-year-old Rohit Kumar from Bihar, India, fell into the lake near Tal Barahi Temple while visiting Pokhara with friends. Rescue personnel stationed at a nearby Armed Police Force monitoring tower responded immediately but failed to save him.

Five days later, the body of 50-year-old Bir Bahadur Rai, originally from Sindhuli and living in Ratnachowk, Pokhara, was found floating near the lakeshore.

Whenever emergencies occur on Phewa Lake, rescue teams from the APF Kalika Battalion are deployed. Personnel from the 24th Battalion operate round-the-clock from the Phewa Watch and Rescue Tower at Barahighat.

According to battalion records, 28 major water-related incidents occurred in the 2025-26 fiscal year. These included wooden boats, kayaks and stand-up paddleboards capsizing because of sudden winds or human negligence, as well as drowning incidents and people entering the water in risky circumstances. Rescue teams saved 85 people, but eight people died.

Inspector Binod Paudel, chief of the Gandaki Province Disaster Management Team under the APF, said 20 personnel work in two shifts at the rescue tower daily. At least three deep-water divers remain on standby at all times.

However, rescue capacity has not matched the increasing number of recreational activities on the lake.

Data from the Kaski District Police Office show nine people drowned in Phewa Lake in fiscal year 2023-24 and four in 2024-25. Five of those who died in the latter year were children.

Kumar Pariyar of Pumdibhumdi, who has operated wooden boats on Phewa Lake for more than a decade, says he has witnessed the risks created by the rapid growth of stand-up paddleboarding.

According to him, many young users venture into the lake alone, remove life jackets while swimming or enter the water after consuming alcohol.

“Many people take these boards out without understanding the risks. A small gust of wind can overturn them,” Pariyar said. “If someone does not know how to swim, they can disappear under the water within seconds.”

He added that during storms, traditional wooden boat operators often assist APF rescue teams in saving people stranded in the lake.

Balaram Giri, chairman of the Phewa Boat Entrepreneurs’ Committee, said 767 wooden boats and 72 large motor-assisted boats operate under the official committee. However, hundreds of stand-up paddleboards are now available for rent through 42 operators, including private rental companies, hotels and lakeside restaurants.

Neither the local administration nor Pokhara Metropolitan City has an exact record on how many paddleboards are available to use on the lake.

A paddleboard can be rented for as little as Rs200 per hour. Giri said only five of the 42 operators have obtained permits from the local government.

“Stand-up paddleboards are unstable by nature. Even a small wave can overturn them,” Giri said. “The bigger problem is that they operate without proper monitoring. The metropolitan city has failed to introduce clear operating guidelines, and the sector has grown largely unregulated.”

Stand-up paddleboarding was introduced to Phewa Lake around seven or eight years ago by Paddle Nepal. But its popularity surged sharply over the past two years, with operators expanding across the lakeside area.

Assistant Chief District Officer Chitrangad Baral said the administration intervened after receiving repeated complaints about unregistered water sports businesses, lack of price lists, failure to provide receipts, absence of safety insurance and unsafe operating practices.

The June 25 directive required all water sports operators to register and renew permits before continuing operations. It also made life jackets compulsory for every user.

Operators must provide customers with safety briefings covering basic navigation, possible hazards and emergency procedures before allowing them onto the water. They are prohibited from serving people under the influence of alcohol or drugs and must refuse service to anyone appearing intoxicated.

The rules also prohibit children aged 16 and below from using paddleboards or boats without adult supervision. Operators must maintain continuous visual contact with customers and ensure immediate rescue assistance in case of emergencies.

To address monsoon-related risks, the administration has prohibited boating, kayaking, and surfing after 2 pm during adverse weather conditions. All water tourism activities must stop after 6 pm every day.

Compliance remains weak.

Deputy Superintendent of Police Namraj Bhattarai of the Baidam Ward Police Office acknowledged that many operators continue to ignore safety requirements.

“We have repeatedly detained operators violating safety protocols and released them after they signed written commitments,” Bhattarai said. “Many recent accidents have occurred because people enter the water after consuming alcohol.”

Pokhara Metropolitan City Mayor Dhanraj Acharya said the city has drafted a Water Transport Act to regulate recreational activities on the lake.

“The act will come into force within a few days after its publication in the official gazette,” Acharya said. “We believe strict registration requirements, clear standards, and active regulation will help reduce accidents.”

For now, Phewa Lake continues to draw visitors seeking adventure, but the absence of effective monitoring has turned a popular recreational activity into a growing public safety concern.

articles.title: America slips further out of reach for many aspiring Nepalis
articles.summary:
Eva Bhattarai (name changed on request) had hoped to travel to the United States for one simple reason: To attend her daughter’s graduation in 2027. However, a new US State Department rule requiring some B1/B2 visa applicants to deposit a refundable bond of up to $20,000 before traveling has left that wish out of reach.

“No matter how much I want to go, I cannot set aside that much money,” Bhattarai, a resident of Baneshwar, Kathmandu, says.

She is among many Nepalis reassessing their travel plans after the US Department of State announced that its visa bond programme, first introduced as a 12 month pilot in August 2025, would become permanent from Monday.

Under the programme, consular officers may require selected B1/B2 visa applicants from around 50 countries, including Nepal, to deposit US$10,000, US$15,000 or US$20,000 before a visa is issued. Although US$15,000 is expected to be the standard amount, officers can require a lower or higher bond depending on factors such as the applicant's purpose of travel, employment, income, and other circumstances.

The bond is refundable if travellers comply with US immigration rules and leave before their authorised stay expires.

For Bhattarai, the policy has effectively ended her plans to visit her daughter.

“I want to visit my daughter, not settle there,” she says, describing the proposal as unfair. “By the time families prepare according to one set of rules, another policy is already announced.”

The new proposed plan has already begun shaping how some Nepalis think about future travel to the United States. For instance, parents hoping to visit children, repeat visitors and business travellers all say the financial burden could alter their travel plans, even though the money would be refunded upon compliance with visa conditions.

For many citizens of a country with an average annual income of around $1,500, having to provide such a substantial deposit—even a refundable one—creates a major obstacle and makes the possibility of travel far less certain. The minimum deposit amount is several times greater than the country’s annual per capita income.

Koteshwar resident Leela Bhandari, 53, whose son has lived in the US for seven years, said the rule did not affect her recent trip because her visa had already been issued before the programme was announced. Still, she says, she found the idea difficult to accept because applicants could be required to pay a large sum before knowing whether their visa would even be approved.

“It would only make sense if the bond were collected after the visa was confirmed,” she says. “Otherwise, people could be refused at the interview despite paying.”

Bhandari says she would still travel to the US if the money were refunded after her visit. While she believes the measure is intended to discourage overstaying and ensure travellers return home, she says it is unreasonable to require such a large financial commitment before a visa decision has been made.

Fifty-five-year-old Deepak Joshi (name changed on request), who has a son and daughter who have both lived in the US for the past decade, expressed a similar concern, saying the proposal was not a good policy, particularly for people from poorer countries. However, the Bhaktapur resident acknowledged that every nation has the right to set its own immigration policies.

“If the money is refundable, I would still travel,” he says. Joshi said that the measure appeared to be aimed at controlling the number of foreign visitors and managing immigration more strictly. “It is the US government’s policy,” he says. “People who want to visit will have to comply.”

Among repeat visitors, the policy has also raised questions about future travel.

Riti Dawadi (name changed), 26, who works in the IT sector, has travelled to the US three times to visit family and for holidays, says her current visa remains valid until 2028, so the rule will not immediately affect her. But she said it has already made her think differently about future trips.

“Earlier, I could just book a ticket and go," she says. “Now, depositing such a large amount of money will make it much less straightforward.”

Dawadi says the policy seems somewhat unfair, even if she understood that countries have the right to set their own rules. She also worries that travellers could lose the deposit if something unexpected happened and they overstayed unintentionally.

“The measure could also discourage tourism to the US by reducing the number of visitors”, says Dawadi.

Business travellers see a more nuanced picture.

Fifty-two-year-old Raj Pokharel (name changed on request), who heads a Kathmandu based-think tank working on security and governance and expects to travel to the US next year for a business programme, says the requirement would create an additional financial burden but would not necessarily prevent essential travel.

“Even though arranging a large refundable bond would create an added burden, I would still travel to the US if the meetings were important”, says Pokharel. He believes the policy is intended to address visa misuse, including overstaying or changing immigration status after arrival.

“Many genuine travellers do return,” he says, adding that the policy would hurt people who have no intention of overstaying but lack the resources to deposit a large sum.

He says the rule could also reduce the number of Nepalis traveling to the US, especially among families, young people and first time visitors.

articles.title: Q&A: Fluid organisational structures were used to propagate religious hate
articles.summary:
In the wake of social unrest in the Tarai-Madhesh region, triggered by a communal clash in Devanganj, Sunsari on July 26, Nepal finds itself grappling with a recurring vulnerability to communal friction along religious lines. While authorities have routinely leaned on coercive force to quell violence, critics argue that such reactive measures fail to address the deeper, systemic undercurrents fueling the crisis.

The Post’s Biken K Dawadi sat down with political scientist and commentator Bhaskar Gautam to dissect the complex historical and socio-political roots of these tensions. Gautam offers a critical perspective on how decades of secular popular mobilisation have historically contrasted with a Hinduised state structure, and how external religious networks and fluid digital campaigns continue to exploit socio-economic vulnerabilities. The conversation probes the state’s governing mentality, the limits of police and security sector reforms, and the urgent necessity for transparent institutional dialogue to preserve social harmony.

How did the communal tensions within the Tarai-Madhesh region of Nepal evolve over time?

In the specific case of Nepal, and the Tarai-Madhesh belt in particular, the background of communal riots must be understood through several distinct contexts. If we compare our situation to India at a political level, the first point of note is that the historical nature of political mobilisation in Nepal has been a secular space. Since the 1950 revolution, modern Nepali politics was mobilised—perhaps by design or perhaps by coincidence—in a manner that was fundamentally different from the Indian experience.

In what sense?

Both BP Koirala and Pushpa Lal Shrestha established a foundation for political mobilisation that was entirely distinct from India’s, as it lacked a religious component. Consequently, from its inception, whether through party politics or modern forms of collective action, Nepal operated within a secular space. In many ways, I believe this is a lesson that Nepal could even teach India. However, while our political mobilisation was secular, we must acknowledge that the state itself was not. If we examine the state as an entity, it remains a Hinduised structure. This creates a core tension in our seventy years of democratic imagination: Secular mobilisation has consistently stood in opposition to a Hinduised state structure, yet many observers frequently conflate these two distinct elements when discussing the politics of religion in Nepal.

Until what point did this secular form of popular mobilisation remain the dominant force in Nepali society?

This secular form of popular mobilisation remained the primary mode of engagement in Nepal nearly up until the promulgation of the 2015 Constitution. I maintain this distinction between the secular nature of popular movements and the non-secular nature of the state. It was only after the constitution was established that we saw significant shifts, notably when KP Sharma Oli attempted to instrumentalise religion for political mobilisation. Although his initial attempts were largely unsuccessful due to the specific context of the time, the efforts to move in that direction were clearly present. In the decade since then, the expansion of religious influence within society has become widespread.

What were the early signals of religious influence entering the Nepali political landscape from external sources?

If we discuss the politics of religion, which is inextricably linked to current communal tensions, we can trace a thread back to the period following the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi by Nathuram Godse. When the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) was briefly banned in India, they looked outward to expand their activities, and Nepal was part of that first phase of expansion. During the 1950s and 60s, many teachers arrived from India to work in Nepal, and some were involved in expanding RSS activities. The first recorded religious riot in Nepal occurred in Nepalgunj around 1951, involving individuals whom the Nepali government eventually extradited at the request of the Indian government.

How did the activities of the RSS evolve during the subsequent decades leading up to the restoration of democracy in 1990?

From the early 1950s until roughly 1991, the activities of the RSS operated informally under various guises, often led by Indian nationals. This period entered a new phase after King Mahendra took absolute power, as the informal expansion within society became easier and, in some ways, did not require overt public justification. It was only after 1991 that the politics of the RSS took a formal and institutional path in Nepal through the World Hindu Federation. Their methodology followed an established template: Operating through schools, targeting young and impressionable children through their branches, and specifically recruiting talented but economically disadvantaged individuals into a lifelong commitment to the organisation.

Where was the initial focal point for this educational and religious expansion within Nepal?

The first centre for the expansion of these educational and religious activities was the Dhading district, where substantial work was conducted before the movement spread elsewhere. However, over the last decade, we have observed a shift that mirrors developments in India, particularly following the rise of Narendra Modi after the 2002 Godhra incident. We can categorise this into two phases: 2002 to 2014, and the period after 2014. Since 2014, with the BJP in power in India, the RSS has been able to operate freely with massive state resource mobilisation, which has led to a significant expansion of similar activities and networks within Nepal, facilitated by the presence of a Hindu-centric power structure across the border.

What specific events in recent years served as a catalyst for the heightening of communal sensitivities in Nepal?

The Covid-19 pandemic served as a major triggering event in Nepal. During this time, there were attempts to exploit Hindu-Muslim tensions, particularly in Saptari. This manifested through two primary contexts: Tensions surrounding migrants returning from India to quarantine centres and friction with the administration regarding Muslims performing communal prayers. This period saw a significant expansion of hate politics via social media, which has continued to spread in various forms. A notable trend in the last decade is the use of fluid organisational structures. Instead of one static organisation, various groups are formed for specific purposes and then dissolved or rebranded as needed.

Could you elaborate on the strategic reasons behind this constant formation and dissolution of various groups?

This is a strategic choice. While the core actors often remain the same, they emerge under new banners—some focused on sanitation, others on temple construction, and others, particularly in Madhesh, on river conservation campaigns. However, the rhetoric used by these groups is invariably tied to religious and cultural identity. This rapid creation and dissolution of groups, a tactic likely learned from contemporary Indian practices, makes it difficult for researchers or journalists to track their affiliations and funding. Furthermore, during periods of political transition or regime change, dissatisfied political forces often use these long-standing communal triggers to disrupt the peace process or influence the political course, as seen during the 2006 Nepalgunj riots involving pro-monarchy groups.

How would you evaluate the government’s seriousness in addressing these underlying communal currents?

The government’s level of seriousness is a critical question, especially since intelligence assessments reportedly warned three years ago that expanding religious activities could lead to riots. These tensions are an undercurrent with multiple dimensions. We see a pattern where organisations like the Hindu Samrat Sena appear, benefiting from a fragmented structure that allows them to evade scrutiny while maintaining institutional and individual links. Some of these groups, including digital platforms like Men’s Room Reloaded (MRR), have ties to the current power structure. But their ties with Hindu extremist organisations invite scrutiny. But they need to be researched before we reach any conclusion. Questions have been raised regarding the connections between individuals close to the leadership and external political entities, which warrant official investigation.

What does the current administration’s approach to these issues reveal about its broader governing philosophy?

The current government’s mentality is characterised by systemic targeting and selective prosecution. This is evident in how they have handled various incidents and even in their approach to anti-corruption efforts. The administration appears to operate with a ‘command’ mentality, which is essentially an authoritarian or dictatorial tendency. Such a mindset negates the space for democratic communication and dialogue, favouring prosecution and punishment instead. This is dangerous because it shifts the state’s reliance toward the massive and indiscriminate use of force, which in turn encourages their networks to celebrate violence as a form of social punishment. We see this religious underpinning even in the reproduction of values within these networks, such as the Bhajan Mandali campaigns, which reflect a dangerous trend of merging religious zeal with state-sanctioned coercion.

Is there evidence to support the claim that the Police are disproportionately brutal when operating in the Madhesh region?

When a government institutionalises selective targeting, it fosters impunity rather than the rule of law. Nepal has a long historical legacy of impunity that successive governments have failed to undo. In this context, the police do not operate in a vacuum. If a government flourishes on impunity, the institution of the police cannot be expected to function effectively or fairly. Historically, the Nepal Police have been quick to use lethal force in protests across the country, not just in Madhesh—this is evident in the deaths of 19 youths during protests around the capital during the first day of Gen Z protests. This indicates a systemic failure in decades of police reforms and a tendency for ruling parties to treat the police as a tool for political interest rather than a professional, humanised institution.

What role have international donors and foreign aid played in the success or failure of these security sector reforms?

International actors are also complicit in this failure. During Nepal’s conflict years, there was massive foreign investment aimed at reforming security institutions and meeting basic human rights values. For example, significant funding for police reform came from the UK’s DFID (now FCDO), yet the lack of fundamental reform has been raised even in the British Parliament. The evidence from every protest—whether in Tikapur, the Madhesh, or Karnali—shows that these reforms did not lead to a more democratic or sensitive security apparatus. Instead, we see an institutionalised insensitivity that becomes even more blatant and serious when targeting marginalised communities.

How concerning is the apparent involvement of former high-ranking security officials with external organisations that have a religious-political agenda?

The involvement of retired generals and police officials with organisations like the RSS or HSS is a significant dimension of the problem. To understand how this works, we can draw parallels with India, where the RSS operates based on four pillars: strong organisational mobilisation, a clear ‘enemy’ for hate politics, a core ideological orientation, and the mobilisation of power and resources. In Nepal, we see variations of this model where state resources are mobilised for right-wing Hindu politics. This includes strategic access to the power corridors for land acquisition—as seen with various religious outfits—and the recruitment of retired security personnel who possess the tactical knowledge required to manage or manipulate community-level violence.

How do you view the state’s intervention in the communal clashes in Tarai-Madhesh?

I do not believe the delay was necessarily a coordinated plan, but rather a result of a governing mentality that prioritises coercive measures and punishment over dialogue and coordination. This administration’s orientation does not leave it mentally open to immediate crisis management through democratic exchange. There is also a profound distrust between the high-level executive and the institutions they lead, resulting in a situation where leaders feel they must do everything themselves or only through a trusted inner circle. This undermines the autonomous functioning of institutions and leads to parallel, uncoordinated activities during a crisis.

How has this lack of institutional autonomy affected the performance of administrators and police officers on the ground?

Except in cases where a Chief District Officer (CDO) or police chief is exceptionally confident based on their own experience and personality, most local officials hesitate to act without orders from above. While they have the constitutional and institutional space to initiate coordination and de-escalate situations, the system is not built to encourage such discretion. Consequently, they wait for orders, often only receiving them when the situation has already spiralled. When the leadership at the top is more concerned with internal competition than coordination, the response on the ground is bound to be weak.

How do you account for the discrepancy between the reformist election agendas of the ruling RSP and their actions once they attained power?

This is a structural and institutional issue rather than a purely individual one. Once in power, parties often inherit a cultural fabric that values coercion and consolidated traditionalism over democratic strengthening. Furthermore, there is a fundamental flaw in the official understanding of ‘development’ in Nepal, which has historically relied on a trickle-down model and the coercive use of force, leading to displacement and urban slums. Many in government suffer from a form of historical amnesia and ignorance regarding these domestic and international constraints. This ignorance is often masked by individual arrogance—the belief that a few individuals can ‘save’ the country—which systematically undermines the very institutions needed to achieve long-term goals.

What is the relationship between poverty, governance, and the rapid spread of communal triggers in certain areas?

Communal triggers spread most rapidly in areas where poverty is high, superstition is prevalent, and intermediate social institutions are weak. This is directly connected to unemployment, corruption and bad governance. Without institutionalising the rule of law, corruption-free governance is impossible, as impunity can never lead to good governance. Because the government remains largely incompetent and institutions are not in place, state resources are often misused, hindering the path toward a more just and equal society.

In his recent address, the PM appealed to civil society to help maintain peace. Does this suggest a shift in the administration’s stance?

While the PM’s appeal to political parties, civil society and religious leaders to establish peace acknowledges that security cannot be achieved through force alone, this creates a paradox. A government cannot effectively appeal to the ‘associational life’ of a society while simultaneously placing restrictions on press freedom and unions. Furthermore, there is a tendency to blame all of Nepal’s current ills on the post-1990 period, which ignores why the 1990 movement was necessary in the first place. By branding everyone active in politics over the last 35 years as enemies, the government finds itself in the awkward position of now needing the help of those very ‘enemies’ to maintain social harmony.

Given the geopolitical sensitivities and the open border with India, what special measures should be considered for the Madhesh region?

Because these religious tensions are directly connected to developments in India, we cannot rely solely on traditional nationalist rhetoric. We must think about cross-border dialogue that cannot be simply controlled or shut down. We also need to learn from the past. For example, the most effective investigation into the 2006 Nepalgunj riots was an independent commission formed by citizens, not the government. We must empower regional hubs, like Biratnagar or Janakpur, to conduct their own autonomous investigations into communal incidents rather than waiting for Kathmandu to act.

Finally, what role does education play in mitigating these communal tensions?

Education is necessary, but we must note that current communal incidents are primarily occurring in urban or transitional spaces, not in villages. In villages, trust networks are stronger and external mobilisers are more easily tracked. The urban nature of these clashes suggests they are driven by organised actors who exploit semi-educated or semi-literate populations. To counter this, we need informed and critical citizens who can respond immediately to a crisis by opening dialogues with local administrations rather than waiting for the state. If we can foster this proactive spirit and invest in democratic values within the religious sector, we can create a more vibrant and resilient democratic life that does not depend solely on government appointments or official reports.

articles.title: Sunsari crisis shows why consultation matters
articles.summary:
Cocooned within their own circle and relying primarily on the mobilisation of security forces to contain the communal tensions in the Tarai-Madhesh, Prime Minister Balendra Shah and his key Cabinet colleague, Home Minister Sudan Gurung, finally came forward in search of a consultative solution to the crisis. Three lives were already lost, with several others sustaining bullet injuries in days of violence before Gurung descended to Sunsari and Shah addressed the nation on Thursday.

Stepping out of his chamber, Shah not only called on President Ramchandra Paudel for the first time since taking charge as the executive head four months ago, but also telephoned Vice-President Ram Sahaya Prasad Yadav and held a meeting with Madhesh-based parties. Gurung, on the other hand, visited the violence-affected districts, reaching out to victims’ families and negotiating with different communal groups. His determination that he would not return to Kathmandu until law and order is restored deserves applause.

The results of the engagement can already be seen. Life in the clash-affected districts is gradually returning to normalcy, and there have been no reports of violence over the past three days. This also gives every reason to argue that had the prime minister and his team embraced consultation and stakeholder engagement immediately after the violence erupted on July 26, the crisis could have been contained much earlier, with minimal loss.

Nepal has gone through several crises over the years. Each time, political parties have set aside their rivalries and united to find a solution. It is a beautiful political culture that is seldom seen in our neighbourhood. This time as well, representatives of all the parties, in an all-party meeting held by the ruling party, called for peace and restraint.

The response once again demonstrated that Nepal’s political challenges are often best addressed through dialogue and collective ownership rather than through the strength of numbers alone. This is a lesson that remains relevant for the incumbent government as it navigates the crisis and the broader responsibilities that come with power.

Rastriya Swatantra Party leaders and Shah’s ministers often cite the overwhelming number of seats they won in the March elections to defend their moves. While it is true that people showered them with unprecedented support through their votes, it is equally true that the RSP secured less than 50 percent of the total vote share. This means that more than half of the votes were for other parties, even though this did not secure them seats in Parliament. That is also a reminder that the political parties representing the other half of the electorate need to be taken into confidence when making crucial decisions or responding to times of crisis.

The Sunsari violence was a test case for the incumbent government, and it appears that Shah and his team have understood the importance of a consultative approach. And rightly so. Shah should now appear in Parliament and entertain questions from lawmakers. He should also face the media and interact with the general public, as Gurung has done. The position of the prime minister or ministers is not merely administrative; it is political. It demands stepping out of the chambers of Singha Durbar and the four walls of Baluwatar. The Sunsari incident seems to have triggered that much-needed departure, and the country now expects the government to sustain the same level of engagement, if not more, in the days ahead.

articles.title: Madhesh tests Nepal’s secular credentials
articles.summary:
After a week of communal turmoil, Madhesh is finally settling down. The home minister’s crisis management strategy has helped bring leaders of the Hindu and Muslim communities to the talks table. The prime minister’s earnest outreach to political actors in the region, though a tad belated, has helped establish a sense of accountability and fraternity. However, the flames of communalism hardly die down with ad hoc measures. Bureaucratic management of the communal tension must be followed by long-term strategies to address deep-rooted problems, beginning with the concept of secularism itself.

From what we have heard from the media, Prime Minister Balendra Shah is firm in his commitment to secularism. His argument, as his interlocutors put forth, is clear: Any debate on the desecularisation of the Nepali state entails an unviable quest to undo republicanism and federalism. Based on this information, we can rest assured that secularism as a political principle of the Nepali state is in good hands—at least for now. But we cannot remain complacent.

First things first, the timing of the communal tension tells us something about a subterranean effort underway in Madhesh to undo secularism. Certainly, the tensions began with a display of machismo from men belonging to two different communities in Kaptanganj of Sunsari: Hindu devotees on the Bol Bam procession blasting religious hymns at night and local Muslim youths trying to cut the former down to size. Enter the trigger-happy police, and a local brawl explodes into a vulgar display of communal hatred spanning an entire province.

Consultations on constitution amendment are underway at the national level, and this is the right time for anti-secularists to intervene. The signs are already out there: Members of various Hindutva-aligned outfits are in constant negotiations with the home minister, with a prominent demand of a return to ‘Hindu Rashtra.’ The home minister is said to have circumvented this demand, instead committing to more viable outcomes in the immediate run. But the negotiations have veered towards reinforcing a unilateral communal suspicion, including a greater scrutiny of madrassas.

Yes, scrutinise Madrassas, but also mandirs. Incidents in the last few years have shown that communalism is not the prerogative of just one religion or community. Instead, we are too quick to provoke and be provoked: Social media used to share communally insensitive videos; religious processions rerouted through the village of a different community just to provoke. Banke, Dhanusa and Sarlahi have seen similar cases of communal tension in the recent past, reinforcing the belief that the same grammar of communalism is being taught across Madhesh: Individuals from a certain community commit verbal or physical acts that undermine communal harmony, followed by the politicisation of the incidents.
