“Wholesale prices have increased by Rs300 to Rs400 per bag across most varieties,” he said. “Nepal does not produce enough paddy to meet domestic demand, so fluctuations in the Indian market immediately affect prices here.”

Industry representatives also point to recent fiscal measures as another factor driving up costs.

From the beginning of the current fiscal year, the government imposed a five percent Value Added Tax on cargo transport services and a 13 percent VAT on electricity used by non-domestic consumers.

Agrawal said the transport VAT alone adds roughly Rs12 to the cost of every bag of rice before it reaches retailers, while higher electricity costs have increased milling expenses.

The price surge is not limited to grains.

Wholesale data from the Kalimati Fruits and Vegetables Market Development Board show that prices of several vegetables have risen sharply over the past month as monsoon rains disrupted production and reduced supplies.

Long eggplant, for instance, was selling at Rs14.25 per kilogram at the wholesale market on July 1. By August 2, the price had climbed to Rs45 per kilogram, an increase of more than 215 percent.

Bitter gourd rose from Rs25 per kilogram to Rs58.33 during the same period.

Leafy vegetables have recorded even steeper increases.

Wholesale mustard greens increased from Rs35 per kilogram on July 1 to Rs175 per kilogram on August 2, with retail prices crossing Rs200 per kilogram in some markets.

Spinach rose fivefold, from Rs55 per kilogram to Rs275, while broadleaf mustard greens increased from Rs45 to Rs125 per kilogram.

Other vegetables also became more expensive.

Wholesale asparagus climbed from Rs276.67 per kilogram on July 1 to Rs450 on August 2. Bananas increased from Rs226.67 to Rs275 per dozen, while ‘Mude’ red potatoes rose from Rs33.25 per kilogram to Rs50.50.

Only a handful of vegetables bucked the trend. Local cucumbers fell from Rs65 to Rs35 per kilogram, while tunnel-grown tomatoes remained largely stable, edging down slightly from Rs20 to Rs19.83 per kilogram.

Binaya Shrestha, information officer at the Kalimati Fruits and Vegetables Market Development Board, said the seasonal decline in production was the main reason for the higher prices.

“Vegetable production declines during the monsoon, resulting in lower arrivals at wholesale markets,” Shrestha said. “Demand remains relatively stable, but supply falls, creating upward pressure on prices.”

He said the current period marks the transition between summer and winter vegetable production, while persistent rainfall has affected yields in many growing areas.

“Summer crops are nearing the end of their season, while winter vegetables have not yet entered the market,” Shrestha said. “In many hilly districts, vegetable cultivation has declined, and farmers in the Tarai are occupied with paddy transplantation.”

He added that tunnel farming had helped maintain the supply of tomatoes and cucumbers, preventing significant price increases in those crops.

Shrestha said there had been no prolonged highway closures caused by landslides in recent weeks, suggesting that reduced production rather than transport disruptions had been the main driver of the price increases.

The pressure on household budgets extends beyond vegetables.

Egg prices, which dropped sharply after outbreaks of avian influenza triggered panic selling, have rebounded in recent weeks.

Wholesale prices have increased by Rs30 per crate. Large eggs now sell for Rs530 per crate, up from Rs500, while medium-sized eggs have increased from Rs470 to Rs500. Extra-large eggs have risen from Rs515 to Rs545 per crate.

Before the bird flu outbreak, large eggs were selling for Rs535 per crate. Prices later fell to Rs475 as farmers rushed supplies into the market. Retail prices have now climbed to around Rs600 per crate.

Producers say the market is gradually returning to normal as poultry farms recover from the impact of the disease, but they do not expect prices to fall significantly in the short term because feed, transportation and production costs remain high.

Consumer rights campaigners say the continuing increases in the prices of essential goods underscore long-standing weaknesses in Nepal’s market regulation system.

They argue that while seasonal factors and import costs influence prices, inadequate monitoring has made it difficult to distinguish between genuine cost increases and excessive mark-ups by traders. They have urged the government to intensify market inspections, monitor supply chains more closely and act against businesses found manipulating prices ahead of the festive season.

With demand expected to rise further in the coming weeks, many households fear the burden of maintaining even a basic kitchen will become heavier unless supplies improve and prices stabilise.

Despite the rise in retail prices, poultry farmers say they are still struggling to recover production costs as the sector continues to feel the impact of avian influenza outbreaks.

Binod Pokharel, president of the Nepal Layers Poultry Farmers Association, said the market is facing a structural supply shortfall after more than 1.2 million laying hens were culled during bird flu outbreaks.

“As a result, national production has been unable to keep pace with demand,” Pokharel said. He rejected claims that current prices amount to excessive profiteering, noting that egg prices had climbed as high as Rs750 per crate three years ago.

“Farmers currently sell eggs at around Rs500 per crate at the farm gate,” he said. “To cover feed and operating costs, the farm-gate price should be at least Rs573 per crate.”

According to the association, Nepal consumes between three million and four million eggs a day, while current production stands at between 2.9 million and 3 million eggs.

Consumer rights advocates say meat prices have also increased sharply in recent months.

Following the bird flu outbreak, the retail price of goat meat rose from around Rs1,250-1,300 per kilogram to between Rs1,700 and Rs1,750 per kilogram. Consumer rights activists argue that such increases, despite relatively subdued demand, warrant closer scrutiny by market regulators.

The upward trend extends to other household essentials.

Refined sugar is currently retailing at around Rs115 per kilogram, while edible oil prices have also risen across the market.

According to the Nepal Retail Trade Association, sunflower oil is selling at around Rs290 per litre in both the wholesale and retail markets, while soybean oil is priced at Rs285 per litre.

Price lists published by the state-owned Food Management and Trading Company show sunflower oil selling at Rs300 per litre and soybean oil at Rs285 per litre, placing the state retailer’s sunflower oil above the prevailing market price.

Rajesh Kumar Agrawal, former president of the Confederation of Nepalese Industries, attributed the rise in edible oil prices to higher international costs.

“Raw edible oil prices in international markets have increased, the US dollar has appreciated against the Nepali rupee and international freight charges have also risen,” Agrawal said. “When costs increase throughout the supply chain, domestic prices inevitably follow.”

Retailers, however, say they are merely passing on higher procurement costs.

Amul Kaji Tuladhar, general secretary of the Nepal Retailers Association, said neighbourhood grocery stores have little influence over pricing.

“Retailers do not increase prices arbitrarily,” Tiwari said. “We buy goods at higher prices from manufacturers and wholesale importers and adjust retail prices accordingly. The government should examine why industrial producers and importers are increasing their prices.”

As households grapple with rising food costs, consumers in Kathmandu Valley are also facing shortages of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), forcing many to queue for hours in search of cooking fuel.

With demand rising and panic buying spreading, the state-owned Nepal Oil Corporation (NOC) began direct sales of LPG cylinders from its central office in Teku, Kathmandu, on Saturday.

Long queues formed outside the depot as consumers carrying empty cylinders waited to exchange them for refilled cylinders of Nepal Gas, HP, Everest, Sugam and Shreeram Gas.

The current shortage has its roots in supply management measures introduced earlier this year.

On March 13, amid concerns over global supply chains linked to tensions in West Asia and volatility in international energy markets, the NOC introduced a quota system under which consumers were supplied only half-filled cylinders weighing 7.1 kilograms.

After receiving assurances from Indian suppliers that supplies had stabilised, the corporation lifted the restriction on July 15 and resumed the distribution of standard 14.2-kilogram cylinders.

According to Manoj Kumar Thakur, spokesperson for the NOC, the shift back to full cylinders created an unexpected surge in demand.

During the four months in which half-filled cylinders were distributed, many households delayed replacing their cylinders in anticipation of the return of full-sized refills.

Monthly LPG consumption in Nepal generally ranges between 45,000 and 46,000 tonnes, Thakur said.

When full cylinders became available again, households returned large numbers of empty cylinders simultaneously, putting pressure on bottling plants and dealers.

“Thousands of empty cylinders entered the distribution system at once, exhausting available stocks at dealer outlets,” Thakur said. “The shortage has been driven mainly by panic buying rather than any disruption to imports.”

He said supplies from the Indian Oil Corporation continue without interruption and expressed confidence that LPG distribution across Kathmandu Valley would return to normal within seven to ten days.

To ease public concern, the NOC has been distributing between 100 and 150 cylinders a day directly from its Teku depot.

Consumer rights advocates, however, say the difficulties surrounding food prices and cooking gas highlight broader weaknesses in market regulation.

Madhav Timalsina, president of the Consumer Rights Research Forum, questioned claims that global factors alone explain the sustained rise in the prices of essential goods.

“There is no convincing economic basis for continuous increases in the prices of rice, pulses, vegetables, eggs and meat,” Timalsina said. “International supply chains have largely stabilised, and tensions in West Asia have eased compared with earlier months. Weak market regulation and ineffective monitoring are allowing prices to rise unchecked.”

Timalsina also criticised the government's enforcement of transport pricing.

He noted that although the Department of Transport Management announced a two percent reduction in inter-provincial public transport fares effective July 2, following a fall in diesel prices from Rs235.83 to Rs193.83 a litre on July 1, many transport operators have continued charging the previous fares.

He further argued that the government’s decision to impose a 5 percent VAT on freight transport services and a 13 percent VAT on non-domestic electricity from the start of the current fiscal year has been used to justify broader increases in retail prices.

“When the state focuses on collecting revenue but fails to monitor markets, inspect wholesale traders or act against hoarding and price manipulation, consumers ultimately bear the cost,” Timalsina said. “With the festive season approaching, stronger market oversight is urgently needed to protect households already under severe financial pressure.”

articles.title: ‘टिकट नपाउदा 'गौँथली'का दर्शक विदेशी सिनेमा हेर्न बाध्य छन्’
articles.summary:
चलचित्र ‘गौँथली’को १७ औँ दिनमा पनि व्यापार उस्तै छ। देशभरका शो हाउसफूल छन्। आइतबार दिउँसोका शो बिहानै र अबेर साँझका शो दिउँसो चाँडै हाउसफूल भए।

अग्रिम बुकिङबाटै शो हाउसफूल भएपछि डोर सेलमा टिकट दर्शकले पाएनन्। हलमै गएर टिकट काटेर ‘गौँथली’ हेर्न पुगेका दर्शक निराश भएर फर्किन बाध्य भए।

सबै हलका अधिकांश शो हाउसफूल हुँदा एउटा हलमा टिकट नपाएका दर्शक अर्को हलमा गएर पनि सिनेमा हेर्न नपाएको वितकर करण श्रेष्ठ बताउँछन्।

‘आज सबैतिर ‘गौँथली’ हाउसफूल भयो। जति दर्शकले सिनेमा हेर्नु भयो त्यति नै संख्यामा त दर्शक टिकट नपाएर फर्किनु भयो। हाम्रो सिनेमाको ओभरफ्लो दर्शक अरु सिनेमाले पाए,’ वितरक श्रेष्ठले भने, ‘प्रायः बलिउडका ठूला सिनेमा नेपाल आउँदा ओभरफ्लो दर्शक तान्न नेपाली सिनेमा लगाउँछन् भनिन्छ, तर यसपटक उल्टो भयो। ‘गौँथली’ हेर्न टिकट नपाएका दर्शक अरु सिनेमा हेर्न गएको पाइयो।’

निर्देशक डा. कपिल रिजाल आइतबार अधिकांश शो टिकट फिलिङ फास्टमा गएको बताउँछन्। दर्शक टिकट नपाएर फर्किएको उनको गुनासो छ।

‘हाम्रो चलचित्र प्रायः हलमा डोर सेल टिकट बिक्री हुने सिनेमा हो। तर, अग्रिम बुकिङमै टिकट नपाउँदा दर्शक निराश भएर फर्किएको देखियो,’ निर्देशक रिजाल भन्छन्, ‘हामी हाम्रा दर्शकलाई क्षमा माग्दै पुनः सहज समय र स्थानमा सिनेमा हेर्न अपिल गर्छौं।’

अधिकांश हलमा एउटा पनि टिकट बाँकी नरही हाउस भएर सिनेमा चलेको उनको भनाइ छ।

साउन १ गतेदेखि प्रदर्शनमा आएको चलचित्र ‘गौँथली’ले आज पनि उच्च अकुपेन्सीमा चलेको छ। प्रदर्शनको तेस्रो आइतबार (हिजो) सम्म देशभरबाट कुल १३ करोड ६४ लाख ४६ हजार ५ सय ३५ रुपैयाँ ग्रस कलेक्सन गरेको छ। यस चलचित्रका ४ लाख ९४ हजार ९ सय १५ वटा टिकट बिक्री भइसकेका छन्।

यस वर्ष प्रदर्शनमा आएका नेपाली चलचित्रमध्ये सबैभन्दा धेरै कमाउने सिनेमा ‘गौंथली’ बनेको छ।

डा. कपिल रिजालको निर्देशनमा बनेको चलचित्रमा अरुण क्षेत्री, सिम्रन खड्का, मदनकृष्ण श्रेष्ठ, प्रकाश घिमिरे, लुनिभा तुलाधर, रवीन्द्र झा, ईश्वरी बराल, सञ्जोग रसाइली, सीतादेवी तिमिल्सिना, लक्ष्मीनाथ तिमिल्सिनालगायतका कलाकारहरूको अभिनय रहेको छ।

articles.title: पार्टी जागरण अभियान सबै पालिकामा सुरु गर्न महासचिव पोखरेलको निर्देशन
articles.summary:
नेकपा (एमाले)का महासचिव शंकर पोखरेलले मिसन पार्टी जागरण पार्टी निर्माणको महत्वपूर्ण अभियान भएकाले सबै पालिकामा सुरु गर्न निर्देशन दिएका छन्।

पार्टीका प्रदेश कमिटीका पदाधिकारीहरू र मिसन पार्टी जागरणका केन्द्रीय प्रतिनिधिहरूसँगको भर्चुअल बैठकलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै महासचिव पोखरेलले उक्त निर्देशन दिएका हुन्। उनले पार्टीको जनतासँग टुटेको सम्बन्धलाई जोड्ने उद्देश्यका साथ सुरु गरिएको यस अभियानलाई सफल पार्न पार्टी कमिटी मात्र नभई जनसंगठनहरू पनि परिचालन गर्ने योजना बनाइएकाले सोही अनुसार परिचालित हुन आग्रह गरे।

पार्टी जागरण अभियान यतिबेला जिल्ला कमिटीहरूका बैठक गरी कार्यक्रम बनाइ अगाडि बढाइँदै छ। पार्टीले पालिका तहसम्म केन्द्रीय प्रतिनिधि खटाएको छ।

महासचिव पोखरेलले पार्टी विस्तारको दायरा फराकिलो बनाउन र वर्ग, समुदाय र पेशागत क्षेत्र समेटेर जागरण अभियान सम्पन्न गर्न सुझाए।

पार्टी सुदृढ बनाउन विचार, संगठन र नेतृत्वमा पुनर्गठन आवश्यक हुने सन्दर्भमा आफ्नो भनाइ राख्दै उनले पार्टी सुदृढ बनाउन विचारधाराको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका हुने हुँदा जनताको बहुदलीय जनवादलाई समृद्ध बनाउँदै आएको स्मरण गराए।

त्यसैगरी, महासचिव पोखरेलले संगठनात्मक पुनर्गठनको काम तलैदेखि गर्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिए। पार्टीका स्थानीय कमिटीहरु चलायमान बनाउने कुरामा ध्यान दिनु जरुरी रहेको र त्यसका लागि कमिटीहरू पुनर्गठन, कमिटीमा रिक्त रहेका स्थान पूर्ति लगायतका काम गर्न उनले निर्देशन दिए।

पार्टीमा युवा सहभागिता वृद्धिका लागि विगतमा युवा परिचालन, युवाको नेतृत्व विकास, युवालाई कमिटीमा आरक्षण लगायत नीति अगाडि सारिएको तर व्यवहारमा लागू हुन नसकेको औल्याउँदै महासचिव पोखरेलले पार्टी जागरण अभियान पनि निर्देशन नै निर्देशनमा समय नगुज्रियोस् भन्नेतर्फ ध्यानाकर्षण गराए।

उनले पार्टीलाई नयाँ ढङ्गले अगाडि बढाउने सन्दर्भमा पार्टीलाई एकताबद्ध बनाएर सुधार र रुपान्तरण गरिने र त्यो काम संस्थागत निर्णयबाट हुने प्रष्ट पारे।

पार्टी सदस्यता नवीकरणको कामलाई सफल बनाउन आग्रह गर्दै समस्या भए पार्टी केन्द्रबाट थप सहजीकरण हुने उनले बताए।

महासचिव पोखरेलले मुलुकको वर्तमान राजनीतिक परिस्थितिबारे जानकारी गराउँदै शासकीय अनुभव नभएका मानिसहरू सरकारमा पुगेकाले देश यतिबेला सङ्कटको अवस्थामा गुज्रिरहेको र विभिन्न स्वार्थ समूहहरूले आफ्नो सक्रियता बढाइरहेको बताए।

उनले सरकार सुरुदेखि पूर्वाग्रह र प्रतिशोधपूर्ण ढङ्गले अगाडि बढेको र यतिबेला नियम कानुन लत्याएर स्वेच्छाचारी शासन व्यवस्थातिर उन्मुख रहेकाले कुनै पनि बेला सडक आन्दोलनमा जानुपर्ने हुँदा तयार हुन पनि मातहत कमिटीलाई निर्देशन दिए।

भर्चुअल बैठकमा पार्टीका सचिव तथा संगठन विभाग प्रमुख भानुभक्त ढकालले पार्टी सदस्यता नवीकरणको प्रारम्भिक रिपोर्टबारे जानकारी गराउँदै नवीकरणको काम उत्साहप्रद रहेको बताए। उनले सदस्यता नवीकरणको समयसीमा असार मसान्तसम्म रहे पनि यो पार्टी कामको महत्वपूर्ण पाटो भएकाले यस कामलाई निरन्तरता दिनुपर्ने बताए।

बैठकमा प्रदेश अध्यक्षहरूले मिसन पार्टी जागरण अभियान, पार्टी सदस्यता नवीकरण लगायत विषयमा रिपोर्टिङ गरेका थिए।

articles.title: मधेसमा चहलपहल बढ्दै
articles.summary:
अशान्त मधेस प्रदेशमा क्रमशः चहलपहल बढ्दै गएको छ।

सिरहाको गोलबजारमा गणेश यादवको मृत्यु भएपछि बिहीबारदेखि मधेस प्रदेश तनावग्रस्त बनेको थियो। गत शुक्रबार गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङ र पीडित परिवारबीच लिखित सम्झौता भएपश्चात् मधेस प्रदेशमा लयमा फर्किन थालेको हो। धनुषा, सिरहा र सप्तरीका केही क्षेत्रमा स्थानीय प्रशासनले जारी गरेको कर्फ्युु तथा निषेधाज्ञा हटेको छ।

उक्त स्थलमा यातायातका साधन सञ्चालन हुनाका साथै बजार सञ्चालनमा आएको छ । स्थानीय विनोद साहले यातायात सेवा सञ्चालनमा आएको र जनजीवन सामान्य बन्दै गएको बताए। सम्बन्धित जिल्लाका स्थानीय प्रशासनले अफवाहमा विश्वास नगर्न र सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम राख्न सबै पक्षलाई सूचना जारी गर्दै आग्रह गरेको छ।

articles.title: बससँग ठोक्किएपछि कार सुनकोशीमा खस्यो
articles.summary:
सिन्धुलीको फिक्कल गाउँपालिका–२, नवलपुर नजिक मध्यपहाडी राजमार्गमा बससँग ठोक्किएपछि एउटा कार सुनकोशी नदीमा खसेको छ।

प्रारम्भिक जानकारीअनुसार कारमा चार जना सवार रहेको अनुमान गरिएको छ। दुर्घटनापछि स्थानीयवासी, प्रहरी तथा उद्धार टोली घटनास्थलतर्फ परिचालित भएका छन्।

फिक्कल गाउँपालिकाका उपाध्यक्ष राजु बरालका अनुसार दुर्घटनामा परेको कार मध्यपहाडी राजमार्ग निर्माण कार्यमा संलग्न कन्ट्र्याक्टरसहितका व्यक्तिहरू बोकेको थियो। घटनाबारे थप विवरण संकलन भइरहेको र उद्धार कार्य जारी रहेको उनले जानकारी दिए।

दुर्घटनाको कारण र सवारहरूको अवस्था सम्बन्धी विस्तृत विवरण आउन बाँकी रहेको प्रहरीले जनाएको छ।

articles.title: ‘टिकट नपाउदा 'गौँथली'का दर्शक विदेशी सिनेमा हेर्न बाध्य छन्’
articles.summary:
चलचित्र ‘गौँथली’को १७ औँ दिनमा पनि व्यापार उस्तै छ। देशभरका शो हाउसफूल छन्। आइतबार दिउँसोका शो बिहानै र अबेर साँझका शो दिउँसो चाँडै हाउसफूल भए।

अग्रिम बुकिङबाटै शो हाउसफूल भएपछि डोर सेलमा टिकट दर्शकले पाएनन्। हलमै गएर टिकट काटेर ‘गौँथली’ हेर्न पुगेका दर्शक निराश भएर फर्किन बाध्य भए।

सबै हलका अधिकांश शो हाउसफूल हुँदा एउटा हलमा टिकट नपाएका दर्शक अर्को हलमा गएर पनि सिनेमा हेर्न नपाएको वितकर करण श्रेष्ठ बताउँछन्।

‘आज सबैतिर ‘गौँथली’ हाउसफूल भयो। जति दर्शकले सिनेमा हेर्नु भयो त्यति नै संख्यामा त दर्शक टिकट नपाएर फर्किनु भयो। हाम्रो सिनेमाको ओभरफ्लो दर्शक अरु सिनेमाले पाए,’ वितरक श्रेष्ठले भने, ‘प्रायः बलिउडका ठूला सिनेमा नेपाल आउँदा ओभरफ्लो दर्शक तान्न नेपाली सिनेमा लगाउँछन् भनिन्छ, तर यसपटक उल्टो भयो। ‘गौँथली’ हेर्न टिकट नपाएका दर्शक अरु सिनेमा हेर्न गएको पाइयो।’

निर्देशक डा. कपिल रिजाल आइतबार अधिकांश शो टिकट फिलिङ फास्टमा गएको बताउँछन्। दर्शक टिकट नपाएर फर्किएको उनको गुनासो छ।

‘हाम्रो चलचित्र प्रायः हलमा डोर सेल टिकट बिक्री हुने सिनेमा हो। तर, अग्रिम बुकिङमै टिकट नपाउँदा दर्शक निराश भएर फर्किएको देखियो,’ निर्देशक रिजाल भन्छन्, ‘हामी हाम्रा दर्शकलाई क्षमा माग्दै पुनः सहज समय र स्थानमा सिनेमा हेर्न अपिल गर्छौं।’

अधिकांश हलमा एउटा पनि टिकट बाँकी नरही हाउस भएर सिनेमा चलेको उनको भनाइ छ।

साउन १ गतेदेखि प्रदर्शनमा आएको चलचित्र ‘गौँथली’ले आज पनि उच्च अकुपेन्सीमा चलेको छ। प्रदर्शनको तेस्रो आइतबार (हिजो) सम्म देशभरबाट कुल १३ करोड ६४ लाख ४६ हजार ५ सय ३५ रुपैयाँ ग्रस कलेक्सन गरेको छ। यस चलचित्रका ४ लाख ९४ हजार ९ सय १५ वटा टिकट बिक्री भइसकेका छन्।

यस वर्ष प्रदर्शनमा आएका नेपाली चलचित्रमध्ये सबैभन्दा धेरै कमाउने सिनेमा ‘गौंथली’ बनेको छ।

डा. कपिल रिजालको निर्देशनमा बनेको चलचित्रमा अरुण क्षेत्री, सिम्रन खड्का, मदनकृष्ण श्रेष्ठ, प्रकाश घिमिरे, लुनिभा तुलाधर, रवीन्द्र झा, ईश्वरी बराल, सञ्जोग रसाइली, सीतादेवी तिमिल्सिना, लक्ष्मीनाथ तिमिल्सिनालगायतका कलाकारहरूको अभिनय रहेको छ।

articles.title: लायन्स इन्टरनेसनल डिष्ट्रिक्ट ३२५ एफको प्रथम क्याबिनेट मिटिङ तथा इन्स्टलेसन कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
लायन्स इन्टरनेसनल एमडी ३२५ अन्तर्गत डिष्ट्रिक्ट ३२५ एफ, नेपाल (लायन वर्ष २०२६–२०२७) को प्रथम डिष्ट्रिक्ट क्याबिनेट मिटिङ तथा क्याबिनेट अफिसर्स इन्स्टलेसन कार्यक्रम आइतवार सम्पन्न भएको छ । डिष्ट्रिक्ट गभर्नर लायन अजय प्रसाद खनालको अध्यक्षतामा सम्पन्न उक्त क्याबिनेट मिटिङमा डिष्ट्रिक्ट भरिका लायन्स लिडरहरू, क्लब पदाधिकारी तथा सदस्यहरूको उत्साहजनक एवं उल्लेखनीय सहभागिता रहेको थियो । बैठकमा लायन्स इन्टरनेसनलको मूल मन्त्र हामी सेवा गर्छौलाई आत्मसात गर्दै चालू लायन वर्षका रणनीतिक योजनाहरू, सेवा गतिविधि, नेतृत्व विकास तथा संगठन सुदृढीकरणका विषयमा गहन र रचनात्मक छलफल गरिएको थियो ।

विशेषगरी, लायन्स इन्टरनेसनलको ग्लोबल कज अन्तर्गतका मुख्य क्षेत्रहरू मधुमेह, दृष्टि, भोक निवारण, पर्यावरण, बाल क्यान्सर, मानवीय कार्य, विपद् राहत र युवा जस्ता विश्वव्यापी प्राथमिकताका कार्यक्रमहरू लगायत डिष्ट्रिक्ट गभर्नरका प्रायोरिटी प्रोजेक्ट तथा मानवीय सेवामूलक अभियानहरूलाई अझ प्रभावकारी रूपमा अघि बढाउने, सदस्यता अभिवृद्धि गर्ने तथा क्लबहरूको सक्रियता र क्षमता विकास बढाउने विषयमा महत्वपूर्ण निर्णयहरू समेत गरिएको छ ।

सोही अवसरमा उपस्थित विशिष्ट नेतृत्वको समुपस्थितिमा नयाँ क्याबिनेट टिमको औपचारिक इन्स्टलेसन (शपथ ग्रहण तथा पदस्थापना) सम्पन्न गरिएको थियो । नवगठित क्याबिनेट टिमले जिम्मेवारी ग्रहण गर्दै आगामी कार्यकालमा समाजमा प्रभावकारी सेवा तथा सबल नेतृत्व प्रदान गर्ने सामूहिक प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेका छन् ।

यस कार्यक्रमलाई भक्तपुर दिबेश्वरी लायन्स क्लबले आतिथ्यता तथा व्यवस्थापकीय सहयोग प्रदान गरेको थियो । उक्त भव्य कार्यक्रमले सम्पूर्ण लायन्स सदस्यहरूमा सेवाभाव, आपसी एकता र समर्पणको भावना अभिवृद्धि गर्दै समाजसेवामा अझ सक्रिय, उर्जावान र प्रभावकारी रूपमा अघि बढ्न ठूलो प्रेरणा दिएको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: Power sharing deal fails to break deadlock in Koshi, Bagmati and Sudurpaschim
articles.summary:
More than a week after the CPN-UML and the Nepali Communist Party (NCP) agreed on July 25 to restructure provincial governments in all provinces except Gandaki and Madhesh, only Karnali has installed a new chief minister. Political disagreements, coalition negotiations and constitutional concerns have delayed government formation in Koshi, Bagmati and Sudurpaschim.

The coalition agreement envisaged the UML leading the governments in Koshi and Bagmati and the NCP taking charge in Sudurpaschim. However, party insiders say internal disputes and difficulties in securing stable majorities have prevented the agreement from being implemented.

In Koshi, the biggest obstacle has emerged from within the UML itself. Party chairman KP Sharma Oli is understood to favour replacing Chief Minister Hikmat Kumar Karki with deputy parliamentary party leader Til Kumar Menyangbo. But several senior leaders have warned that removing Karki could create constitutional complications because he was appointed under Article 168(5) of the Constitution after securing majority support in the Provincial Assembly.

Karki insists there is no justification for replacing him unless the party makes an institutional decision.

"No serious questions have been raised about my performance as chief minister," said Karki. "There is not much time left before the next provincial elections. I believe continuity is appropriate. If the party still wants to replace me, it should do so through proper procedures."

Karki continues to enjoy the support of the Nepali Congress, whose backing enabled him to win a vote of confidence after his appointment. Within the UML, leaders are divided over whether replacing him could trigger constitutional uncertainty and pave the way for fresh elections if a new government fails to secure a vote of confidence.

According to party leaders, Oli has tasked UML secretary and Koshi in-charge Sherdhan Rai with resolving the dispute. Rai confirmed that discussions were continuing but said no final decision had been made.

"We are still discussing whether the current chief minister should continue," said Rai. "The party leadership has asked us to hold consultations before making a decision."

NCP Koshi parliamentary party leader Indra Angbo said the delay stemmed entirely from disagreements within the UML.

"We have already asked the UML to make an institutional decision on its chief ministerial candidate," said Angbo. "Government formation has been delayed because the UML has not resolved its internal differences."

The constitutional debate has become central to the negotiations. Article 168 provides different procedures for appointing a chief minister depending on the composition of the Provincial Assembly. UML leaders fear that replacing Karki without careful legal consideration could complicate the process of forming a new government and create fresh uncertainty in a province that has already experienced repeated political instability.

Coalition seeks RPP, other fringe parties

Coalition partners in Bagmati are focusing on securing a majority by bringing the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) and the Hamro Nepali Party into the new government.

The UML and the NCP have already agreed that the UML will lead the provincial government in Bagmati. In the 104-member Provincial Assembly, 53 lawmakers are needed for a majority. Together, the UML and the NCP command 51 seats.

However, UML lawmaker Apsara Chapagain serves as deputy speaker and cannot vote unless she resigns, making support from smaller parties crucial. UML chief ministerial candidate Jaganath Thapaliya said discussions with the RPP were progressing positively.

"If the RPP supports us, we will have a clear majority," said Thapaliya. "The party has shown a positive attitude towards joining the coalition government."

RPP parliamentary party leader Uddhav Thapa said his party had not ruled out joining the government.

"We have not decided against participating," said Thapa. "The central leadership has yet to make a decision, but discussions are continuing."

Hamro Nepali Party lawmaker Shailendraman Bajracharya said his party was also open to supporting the coalition if negotiations reached a conclusion.

CM Shah's resignation holds up new government in Sudurpaschim

In Sudurpaschim, coalition leaders are waiting for Chief Minister Kamal Bahadur Shah, a Nepali Congress leader, to resign before moving ahead with government formation.

The UML withdrew its support from Shah's government on July 15, leaving it in the minority. Shah subsequently dismissed four UML ministers from his Cabinet. Despite losing majority support, he has yet to step down.

The NCP has already chosen parliamentary party leader Khagraj Bhatta as its chief ministerial candidate.

"The new government can be formed as soon as the chief minister resigns," said Bhatta. "There are no disagreements between the NCP and the UML. We expect the chief minister to facilitate the transition."

Congress chief whip Saraswati Khadka, however, rejected suggestions that Shah was delaying the process.

"The UML and the NCP already have a clear majority," she said. "If they wish, they can stake a claim to form the government. The delay is not because of the chief minister. They may still have internal issues to settle."

The prolonged negotiations underline the challenges of implementing power-sharing agreements despite clear understandings at the federal level. Political bargaining, constitutional concerns and internal rivalries continue to shape provincial politics, reflecting the instability that has characterised several provincial governments since the federal system was introduced.

articles.title: Australia tightens student visa rules, rejects 64 percent of Nepali applications
articles.summary:
Australia has rejected around 64 percent of offshore student visa applications from Nepal, marking the highest rejection rate recorded for Nepali applicants, according to official data.

The surge in visa refusals comes after the Australian government tightened its screening process for international students amid concerns over migration levels, housing pressures and the integrity of the education system.

Australia categorises countries under an “Evidence Level” risk framework to determine the level of scrutiny applied during visa processing. Education sector insiders say Nepal was recently moved to “Level 3”, the highest-risk category, from “Level 2” following a government review conducted several months ago.

The impact has been most severe in the vocational education and training (VET) sector, which traditionally attracts students seeking shorter and more affordable courses. Nearly 90 percent of Nepali applications for VET courses have been rejected, with only 56 of 549 applicants receiving visas, according to recent statistics.

Around 60,000 Nepali students are currently enrolled in Australian institutions. Of them, about 56,000 are existing students, while roughly 4,000 are new arrivals.

Data from Australia’s Department of Home Affairs shows a sharp decline in new student arrivals from Nepal. Between January and May this year, only 2,700 of 7,500 offshore applicants from Nepal were granted visas. During the same period last year, 7,167 of 8,028 applicants received approvals.

The uncertainty surrounding visa approvals, combined with rising application costs, has discouraged many prospective students. Applicants currently have to pay an application fee of A$2,500 (approximately Rs260,000), which is non-refundable even if the visa is rejected.

Sanjeev Pandey, a Sydney-based lawyer, said Australia had welcomed a large number of international students after the Covid-19 pandemic, but authorities later became concerned about patterns of students changing courses and extending their stay without completing their original programmes.

“The government may have also tightened student visa rules to address growing employment and housing pressures,” Pandey said.

The stricter visa regime has raised concerns among education consultancies and smaller institutions that rely heavily on international enrolments.

Khagendra Satyal, international business development manager at Central Australian College, said the decline in student arrivals had significantly affected the sector.

“Visas are now granted only after assessing what positive contributions an international student can make to Australia in the long run,” Satyal said. “Students applying from Nepal need to understand this shift.”

The immigration crackdown also comes amid growing political pressure in Australia over migration. Analysts say the rise of politicians with hardline positions on immigration, including Pauline Hanson, has contributed to a broader political push for tighter controls.

Lawyer Pandey said the tougher environment has affected not only prospective students but also those already in Australia. Renewing student visas, switching back to student visas after completing post-study work arrangements, and bringing spouses as dependants have all become more difficult, he said.

Obtaining permanent residency has also become significantly more challenging compared with previous years.

Despite the tightening measures, Nepal remains one of the largest sources of international students in Australia. Government data shows Nepali students account for around nine percent of Australia's international student population, making Nepal the third-largest source country.

articles.title: बालेन सरकारलाई शिक्षकहरुको चेतावनी: ओली सरकारले गरेका सहमति कार्यान्वयन नभए भदौमा आन्दोलन
articles.summary:
नेपाल शिक्षक महासंघले विगतमा सरकारसँग भएको सहमति कार्यान्वयन नभए पुनः आन्दोलन गर्ने चेतावनी दिएको छ। महासंघको साउन १६ र १७ गते बसेको परिषद् बैठकले माग सम्बोधन नभए भदौ महिनादेखि आन्दोलन सुरु गर्ने निर्णय गरेको हो।

महासंघका अध्यक्ष लक्ष्मीकिशोर सुवेदीले सरकारले विगतमा गरेको सहमति कार्यान्वयनमा बेवास्ता गरे विगतका आन्दोलनभन्दा अझ ठूलो सहभागितासहित सडक संघर्षमा जाने बताए।

शिक्षा नियमावलीप्रति असन्तुष्टि जनाउँदै अध्यक्ष सुवेदीले शिक्षकका माग सम्बोधनका लागि थप छलफल गरी आन्दोलनका कार्यक्रम सार्वजनिक गरिने जानकारी दिए।

शिक्षक महासंघले यसअघि २०८१ चैत २० गतेदेखि काठमाडौं केन्द्रित आन्दोलन गरेको थियो। उक्त आन्दोलन २९ दिनसम्म चलेपछि २०८२ वैशाख १७ गते सरकारले महासंघसँग नौ बुँदे सहमति गरेको थियो।

तर सहमति भएको एक वर्षभन्दा बढी समय बितिसक्दा पनि शिक्षा ऐन जारी नभएको र सहमतिका बुँदा कार्यान्वयन नभएको भन्दै महासंघले पुनः आन्दोलनको तयारी थालेको जनाएको छ। महासंघले अबका कार्यक्रमबारे थप निर्णय गरेर सार्वजनिक गर्ने जनाएको छ।

articles.title: ‘ट्राफिकको उद्देश्य सवारी दुर्घटना कम गर्नु हो, जरिवाना लिनु होइन’
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं उपत्यका ट्राफिक प्रहरी कार्यालयका प्रमुख सुरेशप्रसाद काफ्लेले ट्राफिक प्रहरीको मुख्य उद्देश्य राजस्व सङ्कलन वा जरिवाना असुली नभई सडक दुर्घटना न्यूनीकरण गरी नागरिकको जीवन सुरक्षित बनाउनु रहेको बताएका छन्।

नेपाल यातायात व्यवसायी राष्ट्रिय महासङ्घ, बागमती प्रदेश समितिले सोमबार ललितपुरको बालकुमारीमा आयोजना गरेको सम्मान, पदस्थापना तथा प्रशिक्षणमूलक कार्यक्रममा उनले सवारी चालकले ट्राफिक नियमको पालना गरे कुनै पनि प्रकारको कारबाही आवश्यक नपर्ने स्पष्ट पारे।

प्रमुख काफ्लेका अनुसार ट्राफिक प्रहरीको नियमित निगरानी, सचेतना र नियम कार्यान्वयनका कारण पछिल्ला महिनाहरूमा काठमाडौं उपत्यकामा सवारी दुर्घटनाको दरमा कमी आएको छ।

चालक तथा सर्वसाधारणले अनुशासित भएर ट्राफिक नियमको पूर्ण पालना गरे दुर्घटनालाई अझ प्रभावकारी रूपमा नियन्त्रण गर्न सकिने उनको भनाइ छ।

कार्यक्रममा सहभागी यातायात व्यवसायी तथा चालकहरूलाई ट्राफिक सचेतना, सुरक्षित सवारी सञ्चालन र नियम पालनाको महत्वबारे जानकारी गराइएको थियो।

articles.title: सांस्कृतिक तथा राष्ट्रिय महत्वका चलचित्रलाई साढे तीन करोड अनुदान दिइने
articles.summary:
सांस्कृतिक तथा राष्ट्रिय महत्वका विषयवस्तुमा आधारित चलचित्र निर्माणलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्न सरकारले तीन करोड ५० लाख रुपैयाँ अनुदान उपलब्ध गराउने भएको छ।

सूचना तथा सञ्चार मन्त्रालयले तयार पारेको ‘सांस्कृतिक तथा राष्ट्रिय महत्वको क्षेत्रमा चलचित्र निर्माणका लागि प्रोत्साहन अनुदान कार्यक्रम सम्बन्धी कार्यविधि, २०८३’ को मस्यौदामाथि चलचित्रकर्मी तथा सरोकारवालासँग छलफल गरेको छ।

छलफलमा सञ्चारमन्त्री डा. विक्रम तिमिल्सिनाले मौलिक, यथार्थपरक र राष्ट्रिय पहिचानसँग जोडिएका चलचित्र निर्माणलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्ने उद्देश्यले अनुदान कार्यक्रम ल्याउन लागिएको बताउनुभयो। उहाँले अनुदान वितरण प्रक्रिया पारदर्शी, प्रभावकारी र जवाफदेही बनाउन स्पष्ट कार्यविधि आवश्यक रहेको उल्लेख गर्नुभयो।

मन्त्री तिमिल्सिनाले सरकारी लगानीबाट निर्माण हुने चलचित्रले नेपालको इतिहास, संस्कृति, सामाजिक मूल्य र राष्ट्रिय पहिचानलाई प्रभावकारी रूपमा प्रस्तुत गर्नुपर्ने बताउनुभयो।

छलफलमा सहभागी चलचित्र निर्माता, निर्देशक तथा कलाकारहरूले अनुदान वितरण प्रक्रिया निष्पक्ष र पारदर्शी हुनुपर्ने सुझाव दिएका छन्। उनीहरूले नयाँ तथा उदीयमान चलचित्रकर्मीलाई प्राथमिकता दिनुपर्ने, स्पष्ट मापदण्ड निर्धारण गर्नुपर्ने र अनुदान प्राप्त चलचित्रको गुणस्तर तथा प्रभाव मूल्याङ्कन गर्ने व्यवस्था राख्नुपर्ने धारणा राखेका छन्।

मन्त्रालयले सरोकारवालाबाट प्राप्त सुझाव समेटेर कार्यविधिलाई अन्तिम रूप दिने जनाएको छ। कार्यविधि स्वीकृत भएपछि सांस्कृतिक तथा राष्ट्रिय महत्वका उत्कृष्ट चलचित्र निर्माणका लागि अनुदान वितरण गरिनेछ।

articles.title: बायोग्यास प्लान्ट पुनः सञ्चालनमा ल्याइने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौंको टेकुमा रहेको बायोग्यास प्लान्ट पुनः सञ्चालनमा ल्याउन काठमाडौं महानगरपालिका र वैकल्पिक उर्जा प्रवर्द्धन केन्द्रबीच सम्झौता भएको छ।

महानगरका कार्यवाहक प्रमुख सुनिता डङ्गोलको उपस्थितिमा महानगरपालिकाका प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत सरोज गुरागाईँ र केन्द्रका कार्यकारी निर्देशक नवराज ढकालले आज सम्झौतापत्रमा हस्ताक्षर गरेका हुन्।

सहरमा उत्पादन भएको जैविक फोहर व्यवस्थापनलाई आधुनिक र प्रविधिमैत्री बनाउने उद्देश्यसहित सम्झौता गरिएको हो।

‘सहरमा उत्पादन हुने जैविक फोहरको दिगो व्यवस्थापनका लागि प्रविधिको प्रयोग बढाउने लक्ष्यसहित सम्झौता भएको छ। यो लक्ष्यमा पुग्न निर्धारित समयभित्रै काम पूरा हुने आशा राखेका छौँ’, सम्झौतापछि कार्यवाहक प्रमुख डङ्गोलले भनिन् ‘पुनः स्थापना गर्नु मात्र महत्वपूर्ण उपलब्धि होइन। यसको दिगो सञ्चालन गर्नु र यसलाई सिकाइका रूपमा विस्तार गर्नु उपलब्धि हुनेछ। यो योजना सफल बनाएर सहरमा उत्पादन भएको फोहरलाई दिगो व्यवस्थापनको प्रणालीमा हाम्रो प्रयास जारी छ।’

केन्द्रका कार्यकारी निर्देशक ढकालले आवश्यक उपकरण, सामग्री तथा प्राविधिक सेवाबाट प्लान्ट सञ्चालनमा ल्याउने बताए।

‘यसको अनुगमन र सुपरीवेक्षणपछि महानगरपालिकालाई हस्तान्तरण गर्नेछौँ’, उनले भने, ‘हरित जलवायु कोषअन्तर्गतका कार्यक्रममा महानगरपालिका र केन्द्रबीच सहकार्य हुन सक्छ।’

यो प्लान्ट महानगरपालिकाको एकीकृत दिगो फोहर व्यवस्थापन परियोजनाअन्तर्गत विसं २०७२ मा निर्माण सुरु गरेर विसं २०७५ देखि सञ्चालन थालिएको थियो।

प्लान्ट सञ्चालन गर्दा दैनिक तीन मेट्रिकटन जैविक फोहरबाट १४ किलोवाट बिजुली, ३०० किलो जैविक मल, १३ हजार ५०० लिटर पानी उत्पादन गर्ने लक्ष्य राखिएको थियो।

यसका लागि महानगरपालिका र युरोपियन युनियनले एक करोड ८२ लाख रुपियाँ लगानी गरेका थिए।

प्राविधिक कारणले सञ्चालन हुन नसकेको परियोजनालाई पुनः दिगो सञ्चालनमा ल्याउन गरिएको सम्झौताअनुसार महानगरपालिकाले प्लान्टको दीर्घकालीन सञ्चालन तथा मर्मत सम्भारका लागि आवश्यक बजेट व्यवस्थापन गर्ने जनाएको छ।

यस्तै, प्लान्ट सञ्चालनका लागि योग्य जनशक्ति वा सञ्चालक छनोट गरी व्यावसायिक ढाँचामा लैजाने, पुनः स्थापनापश्चात् संरचनाको पूर्ण स्वामित्व ग्रहण गर्ने गरी वातावरणमैत्री सञ्चालन सुनिश्चित गर्ने, फोहरलाई स्रोतका रूपमा प्रयोग गरी बायोग्यास र जैविक मल उत्पादनमार्फत ‘चक्रीय अर्थतन्त्र’मा योगदान पुर्याउने जिम्मेवारी महानगरपालिकाको हुने बताइएको छ।

परियोजना पुनरुत्थानका लागि केन्द्रले प्लान्टको विस्तृत सम्भाव्यता अध्ययन गर्नेछ। उपकरण खरिद, जडान र परीक्षणको काम सम्पन्न गरेर महानगरपालिकालाई हस्तान्तरण गरिने सम्झौतामा उल्लेख छ।

articles.title: बालेन सरकारलाई शिक्षकहरुको चेतावनी: ओली सरकारले गरेका सहमति कार्यान्वयन नभए भदौमा आन्दोलन
articles.summary:
नेपाल शिक्षक महासंघले विगतमा सरकारसँग भएको सहमति कार्यान्वयन नभए पुनः आन्दोलन गर्ने चेतावनी दिएको छ। महासंघको साउन १६ र १७ गते बसेको परिषद् बैठकले माग सम्बोधन नभए भदौ महिनादेखि आन्दोलन सुरु गर्ने निर्णय गरेको हो।

महासंघका अध्यक्ष लक्ष्मीकिशोर सुवेदीले सरकारले विगतमा गरेको सहमति कार्यान्वयनमा बेवास्ता गरे विगतका आन्दोलनभन्दा अझ ठूलो सहभागितासहित सडक संघर्षमा जाने बताए।

शिक्षा नियमावलीप्रति असन्तुष्टि जनाउँदै अध्यक्ष सुवेदीले शिक्षकका माग सम्बोधनका लागि थप छलफल गरी आन्दोलनका कार्यक्रम सार्वजनिक गरिने जानकारी दिए।

शिक्षक महासंघले यसअघि २०८१ चैत २० गतेदेखि काठमाडौं केन्द्रित आन्दोलन गरेको थियो। उक्त आन्दोलन २९ दिनसम्म चलेपछि २०८२ वैशाख १७ गते सरकारले महासंघसँग नौ बुँदे सहमति गरेको थियो।

तर सहमति भएको एक वर्षभन्दा बढी समय बितिसक्दा पनि शिक्षा ऐन जारी नभएको र सहमतिका बुँदा कार्यान्वयन नभएको भन्दै महासंघले पुनः आन्दोलनको तयारी थालेको जनाएको छ। महासंघले अबका कार्यक्रमबारे थप निर्णय गरेर सार्वजनिक गर्ने जनाएको छ।

articles.title: Gandaki pushes marijuana law through despite federal law concerns
articles.summary:
A controversial bill seeking to regulate the cultivation and use of marijuana for medicinal and industrial purposes in Gandaki Province has finally become law after Province Chief Dilli Raj Bhatta authenticated it on Monday, ending weeks of constitutional debate over the legislation.

Bhatta authenticated the Bill to Regulate and Utilise Marijuana Cultivation for Medicinal and Industrial Purposes after the Gandaki Provincial Assembly endorsed it for a second time without any amendments. The authentication was carried out under article 201 (4) of Nepal’s Constitution, which requires a province chief to authenticate a bill returned for reconsideration once it has been reapproved by the provincial legislature.

The bill had first been passed by the Provincial Assembly on July 9 and forwarded for authentication on July 14. However, on July 24, Bhatta returned it to the assembly with a three-point message, arguing that some provisions contradicted federal laws, including the Narcotic Drugs (Control) Act, 1976, and raised concerns over provincial jurisdiction and coordination with local governments.

It was the first time in the history of the Gandaki provincial assembly that a province chief had returned a bill for reconsideration.

The assembly, however, rejected those concerns. During a meeting on Friday, Minister for Industry, Commerce and Tourism Yasoda Rimal tabled the proposal to reconsider the bill. Following a brief discussion, assembly members from both the ruling coalition and the opposition parties unanimously passed the legislation again in its original form.

Speaking in the assembly, several members argued that article 304(1) of the constitution allows provincial laws enacted under the province’s exclusive powers to prevail, even if they conflict with older federal legislation, after the constitutionally specified transition period.

According to Prabin Paudel, spokesperson for the Office of the Province Chief, the bill was re-submitted on July 31 and authenticated three days later, well within the 15-day constitutional deadline.

With the bill now in force, Gandaki Province has established a legal framework to regulate marijuana cultivation for medicinal and industrial use, with the stated aim of promoting its lawful utilisation, increasing farmers' incomes and encouraging investment in medicinal and industrial processing.

articles.title: Inside Kaptanganj: How a religious flag dispute and a loudspeaker turned a border village deadly
articles.summary:
Om Prakash Mehta was already in bed at around 9 pm on the evening of July 26. But as tensions began rising at the Kaptanganj Chowk, about 700 metres from his home, he watched videos on social media of his own friends at the scene, and decided to go there as well. His father, Krishnadev, tried to stop him, but he didn’t listen.

At around 10 pm, Krishnadev called his 31-year-old son and asked him to come back quickly. “I’ll be there soon,” Om Prakash said, before ending the call. Right then, gunfire erupted at the chowk. Moments later, Krishnadev received a call from one of his son’s friends. “Om Prakash has been shot,” he was told.

By the time Krishnadev ran and arrived at the chowk, Om Prakash had already been placed in an ambulance and taken to the Neuro Hospital in Biratnagar. People there told him it wasn’t very serious and that he’d recover.

Krishnadev changed his clothes and arrived at the hospital, about 25 kilometres east. By then, Om Prakash had been placed on a ventilator. Next morning, his relatives and neighbours told him that the treatment was going well, and he should go home and take care of his wife.

While Krishnadev was returning to Kaptanganj, news of Om Prakash’s death began to spread on social media. His nephew, who was driving, broke the news on their way back.

“As soon as I heard it, I lost consciousness,” Krishnadev recalled. The last time he saw Om Prakash was when he’d left his bed that night, ignoring his plea to stay back.

On the other side of the settlement, west of Om Prakash’s house and about 100 metres south of Kaptanganj Chowk, lives 72-year-old Mohammad Tahir Miyan.

On the afternoon of July 27, a day after tensions began in town, a curfew had already been imposed in Kaptanganj. At around noon, an angry crowd of young men with bottles filled with petrol arrived at Tahir’s house. “They began sprinkling petrol and set the house on fire,” he said.Those inside the house managed to escape, but two houses — belonging to his eldest and third sons — and a pile of straw were burned down.

“We had always lived like brothers,” Tahir said, struggling to come to terms with what had just happened over the last 24 hours. Kaptanganj, located in Dewanganj Rural Municipality about one kilometre south of the Indian border, had no history of Hindu-Muslim violence. Om Prakash was killed in police firing. Tahir’s house was destroyed by an enraged mob. The shared account of these two families from two different communities — Hindu and Muslim — is simple: “Nothing like this had ever happened here.”

The dispute that began there eventually claimed three lives. Jay Prakash Mehta, 21, who was also from Kaptanganj, died four days later while undergoing treatment for a gunshot injury. Ganesh Yadav, 15, from Golbazar of Siraha, also died on July 30. Bystanders say he died in police firing. However, in an interview with Kantipur, Home Minister Sudan Gurung denied that the police shot Yadav.

Kantipur’s field reporting, interviews with more than a dozen people, and a review of previous records suggest that the violence in Kaptanganj unfolded amid a wider pattern of simmering religious tensions in some parts of the Madhesh. In recent years, local disputes, social media amplification, political mobilisation, and repeated institutional failures have been contributing to escalation. This time, it had turned deadly.

The Armed Police Force, Nepal’s border security and riot control force, had flagged the risk of growing communal violence some three years ago, especially in the Madhesh region. A senior APF official familiar with the report told Kantipur last week that the force had repeatedly briefed the political leadership on the risks posed by rising communal polarisation, but its recommendations were largely ignored.

The episode also highlights failures at multiple levels — local authorities that neglected early warning signs, security agencies that responded after violence had already broken out, and political actors who largely remained on the sidelines until there were casualties from the conflict.

Kathmandu, however, largely remained passive in the face of violence that broke out in Kaptanganj, with its immediate response limited to reshuffling of police and administrative officials. Curfew came into effect at 7 am on July 27.

In the days that followed, protests spread throughout Sunsari, then to Morang and later to Siraha, Saptari and Dhanusha. Security personnel were deployed in large numbers as local authorities imposed curfews, yet protesters defied the restrictions. As calls grew for Prime Minister Balendra Shah to address the nation and for Home Minister Gurung to visit the incident site, both leaders faced criticism for their response. Neither appeared in Parliament; Shah instead expressed grief over the deadly clashes on social media while Gurung remained in Kathmandu. Shah also skipped an all-party meeting called by his party chair Rabi Lamichhane to discuss the spread of violence across Madhesh.

Dewanganj Rural Municipality, one of the 12 local levels in Sunsari district, lies about 25 kilometres south of the district headquarters, Inaruwa. According to the 2021 census, the municipality has a population of fewer than 40,000, with Hindus making up 86 percent and Muslims 14 percent. This Maithili- and Magahi-speaking region is largely dependent on agriculture. Nearly two-thirds of households use firewood or cow dung cakes for cooking, while only one in 10 households uses LPG gas. Many young people have migrated to Gulf countries or Malaysia, leaving villages with a larger presence of elderly people, women, and teenagers.

The people who appeared on the streets after the night of July 26 were mostly teenagers and young who had only recently entered adulthood. Elderly and responsible members of both communities remain bewildered with what happened.

“How did something like this suddenly happen?” That is the question many are asking as things try to return to normal after a week.

The dispute that eventually erupted into violence last Sunday began about a month earlier. On June 28, the Muslim community celebrated Muharram on public land at Naya Hatiya Bazaar in Kaptanganj after receiving permission from the ward office.

“We have been observing Muharram for 50 years,” said 36-year-old Jabir Alam, a goat and sheep trader. “Earlier there was a Shiva temple here. Now a Kali temple has been built, one temple after another. We do not have a fixed place, and we have celebrated wherever the local government gives us permission.”

On the day of Muharram, the Muslim community planted 40–50 religious flags at the public site, along with Nepal’s national flag. After the festival ended, two religious flags and the national flag remained there, according to Jabir, for another gathering scheduled after 40 days. They removed the rest themselves.

Before the next gathering after 40 days, Shrawan had begun — the month when Hindu devotees worship Shiva, undertake Bol Bam pilgrimages, and visit temples in large numbers. Hindu residents requested the ward office to take initiative to remove the flags placed near the Shiva temple.

“About ten days earlier, after there was a dispute over the flags, I myself went and said — if the flags are causing problems, we will remove them; let’s not create a dispute,” Jabir said. “But the ward chairman and rural municipality chairman did not pay any attention.”

Shatrughan Prasad Mehta, former principal of the local Babuji Basic School, also points to the same failure by local authorities.

“The ward chairman gave land for celebrating Muharram,” he said. “But afterwards, when our boys asked him not to leave the flags there, he paid no heed to the request.”

On July 26, according to Manoj Kumar Pokharel, the local coordinator for human rights organisation INSEC, a group of youth removed the flags that had been placed there earlier and replaced them with new flags bearing images of Hanuman.

That night, Hindu youths preparing for the Bol Bam pilgrimage the following day, gathered near the Shiva temple. They were playing songs on loudspeakers, including “Jai Shri Ram” and “Bol Bam ka Nara Hai, Baba Ek Sahara Hai.”

They planned to travel about 40 kilometres northwest to the Koshi Barrage to collect holy water and return to offer it at the Shiva temple. The loudspeaker installed on a vehicle facing north was turned toward the south, where the Muslim settlement begins about 100 metres away.

According to people from the Hindu community, Muslim youths went there to object to the playing of those songs. People from the Muslim community, however, claim that the songs were played on loudspeakers at a very high volume toward the Muslim settlement located south of the Shiva temple, and that 8 to10 motorcycles with Indian number plates were repeatedly riding through the road, creating fear among them.

Soon, tensions escalated, a verbal confrontation began, followed by a physical clash. There is no single account of what happened next.

People from the Hindu community say that Muslim youths, who had come in greater numbers than the Hindu youths, started beating them and when they got beaten back, the Muslim youths themselves informed the police. Members of the Muslim community say they did not beat anyone but informed the police after sensing that the dispute could escalate.

Based on details gathered through their field investigation, INSEC’s Pokharel said that the boys from the Hindu side were fewer in number. “Initially, they were beaten,” he said. “Then some among them exaggerated the incident and sought support from the village.”

By then, the police had arrived. “After the police told them to leave, the Muslim youths went home. But the Hindu youths refused to return, saying they had been beaten and wanted revenge,” Pokharel said. “They tried to move toward the Muslim settlement, and then there was a clash with the police who tried to stop them.”

Jabir’s account is broadly consistent with Pokharel’s version.

“The police stopped us in our own neighbourhood, and after that we did not go anywhere. The police stopped them from coming here from the north. During the pushing and shoving, they clashed with the police,” he said. “There was no Hindu-Muslim fight. There was a clash between them and the police. Not a single person from the Muslim side was injured. There are only 50–60 Muslim households here, while they are in the hundreds. How can we survive by fighting them here?”

Although an incident like the one in Kaptanganj had not been seen before, a review of records from previous years shows that the surrounding region has had some history of tensions linked to religious disputes.

According to INSEC records, seven such incidents have been recorded in Sunsari alone — three in 2024, two in 2025, and two so far in 2026. Publicly available reports show that such incidents have occurred from Sunsari westward through Madhesh districts all the way to Nepalgunj.

Kantipur found records of at least 17 such incidents in the Terai over an eight-year period, from 2018/19 until now. Since this list is based only on incidents reported in the media, it represents the minimum number. These incidents occurred in districts ranging from Banke in the west, to Parsa in the centre, and Sunsari in the east. All of these are Terai-Madhesh districts bordering India.

The causes of these incidents also appear to be similar. Around two-thirds of the 17 incidents (11 cases) involved disputes during religious processions and idol immersions held during festivals: immersions related to Durga, Lakshmi, Saraswati and Krishna Janmashtami; processions for Ram Navami and Hanuman Jayanti; Chhath and Kalash processions. In many of these cases, the administration had to impose curfews.

In recent years, social media has become a powerful channel through which local disputes are rapidly amplified and spread. Whether it was an insensitive Facebook post by a Hindu youth in Nepalgunj or an offensive comment against Hinduism by a Muslim youth in Rajbiraj — neither of which Kantipur is linking to or describing in detail — anger that often begins online has started spilling onto the streets.

Chandrakishore, a journalist and author who regularly writes about the Madhesh, believes that the growing access to social media has helped spread tensions rapidly.

“The person who was killed in Kaptanganj had gone to bed. After an allegation or rumour reached him through social media, he came running outside,” he said. “These days videos appear immediately on social media. YouTubers livestream everything, and there is no time for filtering good and bad or right and wrong.”

Incidents deliberately aimed at insulting and provoking another community have also become public. Last year, near the election period in Birgunj, police arrested three people carrying a pig’s head and homemade bombs allegedly intended to be thrown inside a mosque. In Gaur, a dispute occurred after loudspeakers were used during a Hindu wedding procession while prayers were being conducted.

Muslims are Nepal’s third-largest religious group. According to the 2021 census, Muslims make up 5.1 percent of the population. Most of them live in the Terai districts.

The United States Department of State’s 2023 report on religious freedom included complaints from Muslim leaders advocating religious inclusion that they faced pressure from both government officials and the Hindu community.

Dinesh Shrestha, chairman of the Biratnagar chapter of North-South Collectives, a Madhesh-based think-tank, says such disputes that have recently become public are not isolated incidents occurring suddenly or by chance.

“There appears to be an organised effort to increase religious conflict in Nepal,” he said, without identifying those whom he believed were responsible for fomenting such conflicts. “Whether it is incidents that happened elsewhere in the past or the current Kaptanganj incident — all of these have happened as part of that effort.”

Jayaprakash Prasad Gupta, a former minister and the author of the book “Madhesh: Saamajik Samrachana ra Bibhed,” points to the influence from across the border in India.

“In the past, Bihar had governments shaped by caste structures. Now there is BJP’s Hindu-majoritarian politics,” he said. “Nepal too has been becoming polarised under its direct influence.”

Chandrakishore says that four trends seen in growing religious tensions in recent years are reflected in the Kaptanganj incident.

The first trend is the positioning taken by members of the same community elsewhere when an incident occurs in one place. “If something ordinary happens in Malangwa, immediately a procession comes out in Bhairahawa. Earlier, such matters would end locally; they did not spread elsewhere,” he said.

The second trend is the unspoken competition seen in public religious activities in recent years. “If one person puts up one microphone, I have to put up four; if he breaks two swords, I have to break four; if he drives 25 motorcycles, I have to drive 50,” he said.

The third trend, he says, is going in front of another community’s place of worship and loudly raising one’s own community’s slogans as a direct challenge.

The fourth trend is how these conflicts are addressed. Earlier, political representatives played the central role in meetings aimed at reducing social tensions. That space, he says, has been replaced by representatives claiming to speak on the basis of religious identity.

“Suddenly, someone emerged as a Muslim leader, while someone else began attending meetings as a Hindu leader,” he said. “If they had remained in political parties, they might have been ordinary party workers. But now they have become leaders.”

Ram Rijan Yadav, who used to be active in the Janata Samajbadi Party, led by Upendra Yadav, says he has personally witnessed how religious politics from across the border has begun influencing Madhesh. Four years ago, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) had already built an organisation inside their party. “The ‘Yadav boys’ who were part of our party committees had already become associated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS),” he said.

That growing religious polarisation is also visible in the symbols that have appeared across the public landscape.

At Kaptanganj Chowk and along the route west through Biratnagar, Itahari, Inaruwa and into Madhesh, the same image appears repeatedly — on flags, at intersections, outside shops, on rooftops and electricity poles.

The image is of Hanuman. But it is not the traditional depiction of the deity; it is an angry-looking version of Hanuman. The high-contrast image, featuring saffron and black colours and a tightened face, also appears as stickers placed on motorcycles and vehicles.

“The Hanuman I saw while growing up was peaceful,” said Yadav. “For the last two or four years, I have started seeing images of a very angry Hanuman everywhere in Madhesh. The Bajrang Dal and Hindu nationalist groups have promoted this image,” Yadav said.

The image is not rooted in Nepal’s traditional religious iconography. According to reports in Indian media, the ‘angry Hanuman’ image was created in 2015 by Kerala-based graphic designer Karan Acharya. Reports say Acharya designed it for a local temple’s Ganesh Chaturthi festival after friends asked him to create a Hanuman with “a different expression.”

The saffron-and-black image soon became popular across India and later appeared in Nepal as well.

“Culturally and religiously, Hanuman’s image is peaceful. What we have learned is that Hanuman represents knowledge, virtues and humility,” Chandrakishore said. “But for political purposes, Hanumanji was made to appear angry.”

Five days after violence began, the situation in Madhesh began gradually returning to normal following Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s address to the nation, RSP leader Rabi Lamichhane’s marathon meetings, the Home Minister’s field visit, agreements with affected families, appeals by political parties for harmony, and continued dialogue among representatives of different communities at the local level.

But civil society activists warn that if rising religious suspicion among communities is not addressed, the tension may only appear to have subsided while remaining alive beneath the surface, waiting to flare up again.

Curfew has now been lifted in Kaptanganj. Army armoured vehicles stationed at intersections have been withdrawn. Yet, a sense of unease continues to linger over the village.

Both Om Prakash and Jay Prakash had left their homes after learning that tensions had intensified at Naya Hatiya. According to eyewitness Ramesh Kumar Mehta, the crowd became even more agitated after Om Prakash collapsed after being shot by the police.

“People were running in different directions. At that moment, Jay Prakash was also shot in the courtyard of the Shiva temple,” Ramesh said.

In the courtyard of a small hut about 500 metres north of Naya Hatiya, Jay Prakash’s auto-rickshaw has remained parked since the day of the incident.

In Om Prakash’s father’s room, the fan has remained still since Krishnadev left that night after his son was shot.

Tahir Miyan no longer has a house.

articles.title: Rise in king cobra sightings alarms Chitwan buffer zone communities
articles.summary:
An increasing number of highly venomous snakes entering settlements around Chitwan National Park has raised fresh concerns among conservationists, snake experts and local residents, prompting calls for stronger rescue systems and wider public awareness to reduce the risk of deadly snakebites.

Among the most alarming are king cobras and cobras, two of the world's most venomous snakes. Last fiscal year alone, park authorities rescued five king cobras and 17 cobras after they entered homes and settlements in the park's buffer zone.

On June 1, a king cobra entered a house at Barauli in ward 17 of Kawasoti Municipality in Nawalparasi East. The snake was rescued by park staff and released into a dense forest near the park headquarters at Kasara. Another king cobra was found in ward 10 of Kawasoti the following day.

According to snake expert Dev Prasad Pandey, a king cobra bite can be fatal unless treatment begins immediately. Even when victims survive, recovery often takes a long time. However, Pandey says, king cobras differ slightly from other venomous snakes because they do not always inject their full venom during a bite.

“There have not been many confirmed human deaths from king cobra bites in Nepal, partly because they often do not release all their venom,” said Pandey, who completed his doctoral research on venomous snakes in Germany. “But the presence of king cobras and cobras in villages is a serious concern because these snakes are highly venomous and are easily noticed by people rather than hiding from them.”

According to Pandey, cobra bites can become fatal if treatment does not begin within three to four hours.

Park records show that two king cobras were rescued from Kawasoti, two from Meghauli in Chitwan and one from Madi during the last fiscal year of 2025-26.

Abinash Thapa Magar, the park's information officer, said that the snakes had to be rescued after entering villages and residential compounds in the buffer zone. Besides king cobras, the park also rescued 17 cobras during the same period.

Manesh Limbu of Meghauli, Chitwan, has been rescuing snakes from villages for the past 15 years. A professional nature guide, he is increasingly called to rescue king cobras from distant settlements, including Madi.

“I have rescued one king cobra so far this year. Last year I rescued six," said Limbu. “People call whenever such snakes appear because they are frightened.”

Limbu says his knowledge comes from years of working in forests and studying books by Indian snake specialists. He has bought rescue equipment costing between Rs15,000 and Rs20,000 with his own money.

“Even when I rescue king cobras or cobras, I do it entirely on a voluntary basis,” he said. “I earn my living as a nature guide. Snake rescue is not something I do for income.”

People sometimes reimburse his fuel expenses when he travels long distances. The largest king cobra he has rescued weighed 10.3 kilograms and measured 3.35 metres. “When people see such a huge snake inside their yard, they panic. The relief on their faces after the rescue is the biggest reward,” he said.

Thapa Magar said park staff based at the Gharial Conservation Centre respond to reports of snakes and pythons entering settlements. The park also receives help from trained volunteers working through buffer zone forest user committees.

The park is now planning to strengthen its rescue programme with technical support from ranger Yam Raut, who has expertise in snakes.

“Rescue work requires training and proper equipment,” said Thapa Magar. “We have not had a dedicated programme until now, but we plan to develop one.”

Pandey welcomed the initiative but said Nepal still lacked a scientific rescue system. “People are doing rescue work with good intentions, but it needs to become more scientific,” he said. “Rescuers must understand snake behaviour and ensure safe capture, transport and release in suitable habitats.”

According to conservationists and snake experts, snakes usually enter villages between mid-February and mid-October. Pandey informed that forest fires and monsoon floods often force snakes out of forests into nearby settlements. He stressed that authorities should analyse why snakes move into villages and educate communities about seasonal risks and preventive measures.

Chitwan National Park, the country’s first protected area, has long focused on conflict involving tigers, rhinos and wild elephants, which regularly enter settlements around the park. The park launched compensation schemes, rapid response teams and awareness campaigns aimed at reducing human-wildlife conflict. Pandey believes venomous snakes deserve similar attention because they also pose a significant threat to human life.

Last fiscal year, the park also rescued 87 pythons from buffer zone settlements. Although pythons are non-venomous, they are among the reptiles most frequently reported in villages.

Experts urge for better awareness, trained rescue teams, quicker medical response and closer cooperation between the park, local governments and communities are essential to reducing snakebite risks in Chitwan's buffer zone while ensuring the conservation of protected snake species.

articles.title: US resumes humanitarian funding through global agencies after dismantling USAID
articles.summary:
The United States has resumed funding for a range of global health and humanitarian programmes through international organisations, marking a significant shift in its foreign assistance policy roughly 18 months after completely freezing its international aid operations.

Over the past two months, Washington has pledged nearly $2 billion to multilateral agencies working on hunger, infectious diseases, disaster relief and child health, despite President Donald Trump’s continued emphasis on ending recipient dependency on US grants.

The renewed funding comes about 13 months after the Trump administration formally dissolved the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), ending the operations of what had long been the world’s largest bilateral development agency. Instead of rebuilding its overseas presence, the administration is now relying on established international bodies to deliver targeted assistance.

On 20 January 2025, the first day of his second term, Trump signed an executive order directing a 90-day pause on all USAID activities pending a review. The move triggered the temporary closure of USAID offices worldwide, resulting in more than 10,000 job losses.

On 1 July 2025, the administration permanently dissolved USAID as an independent agency, subsuming its remaining functions under the US Department of State.

Last week, the State Department informed Congress that it would provide $600 million to Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, which supports immunisation programmes in low-income countries. The allocation is part of a broader package of humanitarian commitments announced in recent weeks.

The administration has pledged $800 million to the World Food Programme (WFP) to address severe malnutrition in countries including Ethiopia, Myanmar and Ukraine. UNICEF is set to receive $218 million for child health, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene projects.

Washington has also committed $100 million to Operation End Starvation, a public-private initiative aimed at reducing child mortality and severe malnutrition, and $50 million to a coalition developing Ebola vaccines and strengthening pandemic preparedness.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) will receive $203 million for disaster response and emergency assistance.

In addition, the administration has allocated $220 million for Ebola response efforts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and a further $350 million for broader Ebola-affected regions. Another $661 million has been pledged to the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria.

Upon taking office, President Trump claimed that billions of dollars in overseas assistance routinely failed to reach genuine victims, alleging widespread fraud, inefficiency and political bias within USAID. Maintaining that American taxpayers were funding programmes that lacked accountability and produced limited strategic benefits for the United States, his administration ordered the complete dismantling of USAID’s global network.

Sources familiar with State Department discussions told The New York Times that two primary factors drove the policy shift: growing concern over global health security, including Ebola outbreaks, and the practical reality that, following the closure of USAID’s overseas offices, Washington no longer had the operational capacity to deliver aid directly and needed to rely on international bodies instead.

Mark Green, who served as USAID administrator during Trump’s first term, said the administration appeared to have acknowledged the link between overseas health crises and US national security.

“The administration appears to have recognised that global health security is integral to US national security,” Green said.

Jeremy Lewin, the State Department’s senior foreign assistance official, said his team is focused on deploying aid leanly and effectively, with the explicit goal of ending recipient dependency on US grants.

“We will strategically leverage relationships with these international bodies when required, but that does not imply an annual financial commitment,” Lewin said.

Lewin, a key figure in closing USAID and terminating thousands of staff, warned last December that the United Nations risks becoming obsolete if it fails to adapt. While UN Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher publicly supported US efforts to eliminate duplication and improve efficiency, the renewed aid comes tied to strict political caveats.

In December, Washington imposed conditions prohibiting UN agencies from directing US-funded aid to Afghanistan and Yemen, with Lewin asserting that Washington possessed evidence showing aid intended for Afghan civilians had been diverted by the Taliban.

The administration has also reduced food assistance in civil war-torn Sudan and strictly prohibited the use of US humanitarian funds for climate change-related programmes.

Though such politically charged conditions challenge core tenets of humanitarian aid—which dictate that relief must remain neutral, impartial, and strictly needs-based—relief groups note that Washington’s $2 billion pledge provides vital relief at a time when global conflict, famine, and disease are compounding.

Whether the United States maintains that level of engagement long-term remains uncertain, as President Trump declared in 2025 a broader US withdrawal from international organisations alongside foreign aid cuts.

For now, the administration’s latest pledges signal not a return to the USAID model, but a new approach in which Washington seeks to influence global humanitarian efforts by financing multilateral organisations while retaining tighter political and financial control over how US assistance is spent.

articles.title: उद्यमी-व्यवसायीको घर, कार्यस्थलमा छापा मार्ने काम गतिलो होइन : पूर्वअर्थमन्त्री खनाल
articles.summary:
पूर्वअर्थमन्त्री रामेश्वर खनालले उद्योगी व्यवसायीको घर र कार्यस्थलमा छापा मार्ने काम सही नभएको बताएका छन्।

सोमबार बिहान विराटनगरस्थित प्रतिष्ठित औद्योगिक घराना देवनारा समूहका सञ्चालक प्रकाश मुन्दडाको घर र कार्यालयमा प्रहरीले छापा मारेको थियो। करिब साढे ५ घण्टासम्म खानतलासी गरे पनि प्रहरीले रित्तो हात फर्कनुपरेको घटनालाई लिएर विभिन्न कोणबाट टिप्पणी भइरहेको छ।

राज्यले उद्यमी-व्यवसायीलाई सुरक्षा प्रदान गर्नुपर्नेमा प्रहरी प्रशासनको आडमा आतंकित पार्न खोजिएको भन्दै आलोचना भइरहेका बेला पूर्वअर्थमन्त्री खनालले सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत असन्तुष्टि व्यक्त गरेका हुन्। उनले भनेका छन् ‘उद्यमी-व्यवसायीको घर, कार्यस्थलमा छापा मार्ने काम गतिलो होइन!’

व्यापारिक घराना देवनारा समूहको घर र अफिसमा प्रहरीको छापा

प्रहरीले अवैध नगद सञ्चित, हुन्डी र चाँदीको कारोबार तथा कर छलीको आशंकामा सो खानतलासी चलाएको स्रोतले बताए पनि प्रहरी प्रशासनले आधिकारिक रूपमा केही खुलाएको छैन। खानतलासीपछि व्यवसायी मुन्दडाले प्रहरीले घरका सबै कोठा र भकारीसम्म चेक गरे पनि केही नभेटेको र आफूहरूलाई सफाइ दिएर गएको बताएका छन्।

articles.title: पूर्ण स्तनपानले शिशु र आमाको स्वास्थ्यमा हुन्छ बहुआयामिक लाभ
articles.summary:
जन्मेको एक घण्टाभित्र आमाको दूध (स्तनपान) सुरु गरी कम्तीमा दुई वर्षसम्म नियमित स्तनपान गराउँदा शिशु र आमा दुवैको स्वास्थ्य राम्रो रहने परिवार कल्याण महाशाखाअन्तर्गत पोषण शाखाले जनाएको छ। विश्व स्तनपान सप्ताहको अवसरमा शाखाले प्रत्येक आमालाई शिशु जन्मेको पहिलो एक घण्टाभित्रै स्तनपान गराउन आग्रह गरेको हो।

यस वर्ष ‘दीगो जीवनको स्वस्थ सुरुवात, प्रभावकारी स्तनपानका लागि हामी सबैको साथ’ भन्ने नाराका साथ विश्व स्तनपान सप्ताह मनाइँदै छ।

पोषण शाखाका अनुसार शिशु जन्मिएपछि पहिलो एक घण्टाभित्र आउने ‘बिगौती दूध’ (कोलोस्ट्रम) अत्यन्त पोषिलो तथा रोगप्रतिरोधात्मक गुणयुक्त हुन्छ। यसमा संक्रमणबाट जोगाउने इम्युनोग्लोबुलिन, आँखा, छाला र प्रतिरक्षा प्रणालीका लागि लाभदायी भिटामिन ए, भिटामिन ई र के, जिंक, खनिज तत्व तथा ब्याक्टेरियाविरुद्ध लड्ने ल्याक्टोफेरिन पाइन्छ। यी तत्वले शिशुलाई संक्रमणबाट जोगाउने, आन्द्रालाई स्वस्थ राख्ने, पोषकतत्वको अवशोषण बढाउने तथा प्रतिरक्षा प्रणालीलाई बलियो बनाउने काम गर्छन्। साथै स्तनपानले शिशुमा सुरक्षाको अनुभूति गराई मानसिक तथा शारीरिक विकासमा टेवा पुर्‍याउनुका साथै कुपोषणबाट पनि जोगाउँछ।

शाखाले शिशु जन्मेको पहिलो ६ महिनासम्म आमाको दूध मात्र खुवाउन तथा त्यसपछि दुई वर्षसम्म आमाको दूधसँगै बहुपोषणयुक्त ठोस आहार खुवाउन सिफारिस गरेको छ।

परिवार कल्याण महाशाखा, पोषण शाखाका प्रमुख लिलाविक्रम थापाका अनुसार स्तनपानले शिशुलाई मात्र नभई आमाको स्वास्थ्यमा पनि उल्लेखनीय लाभ पुर्‍याउँछ। शिशु जन्मिएलगत्तै स्तनपान गराउँदा सुत्केरीमा अत्यधिक रक्तस्रावको जोखिम कम हुने, पाठेघर चाँडै सामान्य अवस्थामा फर्किने तथा आमा–शिशुबीच भावनात्मक सम्बन्ध अझ प्रगाढ बन्ने उनले बताए।

विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठनका अनुसार शिशु जन्मेको एक घण्टाभित्र स्तनपान गराउन सके ३३ प्रतिशत नवजात शिशुको मृत्यु रोक्न सकिन्छ।

नेपाल बहुसूचक सर्वेक्षण २०२५ अनुसार नेपालमा जन्मेको एक घण्टाभित्र स्तनपान गराउने आमाको संख्या ३८.४ प्रतिशत रहेको छ भने पूर्ण स्तनपान गराउने आमाको संख्या ६९.७ प्रतिशत छ।

त्यस्तै नेपाल जनसांख्यिक सर्वेक्षण २०२२ अनुसार नेपालमा २५ प्रतिशत बालबालिका कुपोषणको समस्याबाट प्रभावित छन्। सर्वेक्षणले ५६ प्रतिशत आमाले पूर्ण स्तनपान गराउने, ५५ प्रतिशत आमाले शिशु जन्मेको एक घण्टाभित्र स्तनपान गराउने तथा ७४ प्रतिशत आमाले दुई वर्षसम्म स्तनपान गराउने तथ्य देखाएको छ। पूर्ण स्तनपानको दर कर्णाली र सुदूरपश्चिममा सबैभन्दा बढी ७४ प्रतिशत रहेको छ भने लुम्बिनी प्रदेशमा सबैभन्दा कम ३६ प्रतिशत रहेको उल्लेख गरिएको छ।

तथ्यांकअनुसार पाँच वर्षमुनिका ४५ प्रतिशत बालबालिकाको मृत्युमा कुपोषण प्रमुख कारण रहेको छ, जसको न्यूनीकरणमा स्तनपान प्रभावकारी उपाय मानिएको छ।

नेपालमा अपूर्ण स्तनपानको समस्या न्यूनीकरण गर्न सरकारले ‘स्तनपान कक्ष तथा स्तनपान सञ्चालन कार्यविधि, २०८०’ लागू गरी सरकारी, निजी तथा सार्वजनिक कार्यालयहरूमा स्तनपान कक्ष निर्माणलाई प्राथमिकता दिएको छ। हालसम्म ६५ भन्दा बढी अस्पतालमा स्तनपान कक्ष स्थापना भइसकेका छन्। साथै जन्मिनेबित्तिकै आमाको दूध पाउन नसकेका शिशुका लागि अस्पतालमा मिल्क बैंक स्थापना, प्रसूति सेवासँगै स्तनपान परामर्शदाताको व्यवस्था लगायतका कार्यक्रममार्फत सरकारले स्तनपान प्रवर्द्धनलाई प्राथमिकतामा राखेको पोषण शाखाले जनाएको छ।

articles.title: श्रमदानबाट साकेलाको अवरुद्ध सडक दुई दिनमै सञ्चालन
articles.summary:
लगातारको वर्षापछि पहिरो र हिलोका कारण तीन दिनदेखि अवरुद्ध रहेको खोटाङको साकेला गाउँपालिका–१ हरेलोडाँडा–साप्सु खोला सडकखण्ड दुई दिनको सामूहिक श्रमदानपछि पुनः सञ्चालनमा आएको छ।

गाउँपालिका अध्यक्ष रविप्रकाश राईको नेतृत्वमा जनप्रतिनिधि, कर्मचारी, सुरक्षाकर्मी र स्थानीयवासीले श्रमदान गरी सडक मर्मत गरेका हुन्। मर्मत कार्यमा गाउँपालिकाको ब्याकहो लोडर, ट्याक्टरलगायत उपकरण तथा स्थानीयले निःशुल्क उपलब्ध गराएको ढुंगा, माटो र ग्राभेलसमेत प्रयोग गरिएको थियो।

गाउँपालिका अध्यक्ष राईले साना पूर्वाधार मर्मतका लागि माथिल्लो तहको बजेट पर्खिनुभन्दा स्थानीय स्रोत–साधन र श्रमदान परिचालन गर्दा छिटो परिणाम प्राप्त हुने अनुभव रहेको बताए। गाउँपालिकाले दुई वर्षदेखि सञ्चालन गर्दै आएको ‘साकेला श्रम अभियान’मार्फत विपद्का कारण क्षति पुगेका सडक तथा अन्य पूर्वाधारको तत्काल मर्मत गर्दै आएको जनाएको छ।

articles.title: डिजिटल हिंसा नियन्त्रण गर्न सबैको सहकार्य आवश्यक
articles.summary:
महिला, बालबालिका, लैङ्गिक तथा यौनिक अल्पसङ्ख्यक र सामाजिक सुरक्षामन्त्री सीता वादीले महिला, बालबालिकामाथि हुने डिजिटल हिंसा नियन्त्रण गर्न सबैको सहकार्य आवश्यक रहेको बताएकी छिन्।

प्रतिनिधिसभा, महिला तथा सामाजिक मामिला समितिमा आज सामाजिक सञ्जालको अवस्थाबारे भएको छलफलमा मन्त्री वादीले सामाजिक सञ्जालको नियमन गर्नुपर्नेमा जोड छन्। उनले बालबालिका र महिला सबैभन्दा बढी डिजिटल हिंसामा पीडित भएका उल्लेख गर्दै साइबर ब्युरोलाई उजुरी प्रणाली सहज र प्रभावकारी बनाउन निर्देशनसमेत दिइन्।

समितिका सभापति आकृति अवस्थीले पछिल्लो समय डिजिटल हिंसा बढ्दो अवस्थामा रहेकाले साइबर सुरक्षाको दृष्टिलाई ध्यानमा राख्दै एकीकृत डिजिटल हिंसासम्बन्धी कानुन निर्माण गर्न आग्रह गरेको छ। सामाजिक सञ्जालको अवस्थाबारे गरिएको छलफल पश्चात् सभापति अवस्थीले भने, ‘डिजिटल हिंसाको अवस्था भयावह हुँदै गएको छ। यस्तो अवस्थामा एउटा एकीकृत कानुन आवश्यक छ।’ उनले कानुन मन्त्रालय, महिला मन्त्रालयलगायत सम्बन्धी मन्त्रालयहरूलाई उक्त सुझाव दिए।

गृह मन्त्रालयका सचिव राजकुमार श्रेष्ठले साइबर सुरक्षा प्रणालीलाई प्रभावकारी बनाउनुका साथै डिजिटल साक्षरतासमेत बढाउनुपर्ने धारणा राखेका थिए। बैठकमा साइबर ब्युरोको प्रतिवेदनसमेत पेस गरिएको छ।

नेपाल प्रहरीका महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्कीले साइबर सुरक्षाको अवस्था जटिल बन्दै गएको बताए। उनले साइबर अपराधको उजुरीलाई तत्काल सम्बोधन गर्न पर्याप्त स्रोतसाधन, जनशक्तिको व्यवस्था र ब्युरो चुस्त दुरुस्त बनाउनुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।
